title: The hit musical of 1728, painted from the theater
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Fugue No. 21, Well-Tempered Clavier Book 1
caption:
In Newgate prison the highwayman Macheath stands in chains while Lucy and Polly beg for his life, Polly kneeling beside her father. Hogarth painted at least six versions of the composition. Look for the little boy peeking out of a box near the man with the sword.

Image: William Hogarth, A Scene from The Beggar's Opera, 1728/1729. National Gallery of Art, Washington. CC0.

#hogarth #beggarsopera #theater #london #arthistory #musichistory

title: The oldest surviving keyboard music, around 1360
caption:
The fragment comes from Robertsbridge in East Sussex and is now in the British Library. Its six pieces are three estampies, a dance form, and three arrangements of motets. This leaf begins 'Tribum, quem non abhorruit'; look for the letters written under the staff.

Image: Anonymous, Robertsbridge Codex, fol. 44r, c. 1360. British Library (Add MS 28550). Public domain.

#keyboardmusic #medievalmusic #organ #musichistory #manuscript

title: Chamber music in a painter's studio, Copenhagen, 1886
caption:
P. S. Krøyer painted friends making chamber music by candlelight in a Copenhagen studio, with listeners packed in close. A study for it was titled after a string quartet. Look for the candles on the music stands and the chandelier glowing above.

Image: Peder Severin Krøyer, Music in the Studio, 1886. Nasjonalmuseet, Oslo. Public domain.

#kroyer #chambermusic #scandinavianart #arthistory #musichistory

title: An empty stool, a waiting viol, and a look straight at us
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Fugue No. 3, Well-Tempered Clavier Book 1
caption:
She turns from the keys to look out at us, as if we are the late duet partner. Look for the red cushion on the empty stool and the wine cooling in a brass basin.

Image: Gerrit Dou, A Woman Playing a Clavichord, c. 1665. Dulwich Picture Gallery, London. Public domain.

#gerritdou #clavichord #dutchgoldenage #arthistory #musichistory

title: The Raindrop Prelude, in Chopin's handwriting
audio_search: Chopin, Prelude in D-flat, Op. 28 No. 15 'Raindrop'
caption:
The nickname 'Raindrop' comes from the A-flat that repeats from start to finish. It is the longest of the 24 Preludes, Op. 28, usually five to seven minutes. This is Chopin's own first page of the piece.

Image: Frédéric Chopin, Prelude in D-flat major, Op. 28 No. 15 (autograph, first page), c. 1838-39. Public domain.

#chopin #raindropprelude #manuscript #pianomusic #prelude

title: The Viennese maker Beethoven, Chopin and Liszt chose
audio_search: Schubert, Sonata in E-flat, D. 568, Andante molto
caption:
Beethoven, Schubert, Chopin and Liszt all owned Graf pianos. The nameplate proudly gives his title as imperial and royal court fortepiano maker. Look at the plain Biedermeier walnut, all about the grain of the wood.

Image: Conrad Graf, Fortepiano, c. 1838. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#fortepiano #schubert #vienna #piano #musichistory

title: Young Sibelius, painted by his brother-in-law
audio_search: Chopin, Ballade No. 4 in F minor, Op. 52
caption:
In 1892 Sibelius was 26. His Kullervo premiered in April and he married Aino Järnefelt in June. Her brother Eero, a painter, made this portrait. Look at the checked jacket and the hands folded in his lap.

Image: Eero Järnefelt, Jean Sibelius, 1892. Private collection. Public domain.

#sibelius #finland #scandinavianart #arthistory #musichistory

title: The first piece in the Eton Choirbook, for eight voices
caption:
The choirbook once held 93 pieces, and 64 survive. Browne is its best-represented composer, and this eight-part setting was placed first. The book is still at Eton College.

Image: John Browne, O Maria salvatoris mater, Eton Choirbook, c. 1500-1505. Eton College (MS 178). Public domain.

#johnbrowne #tudormusic #choirbook #musichistory #manuscript

title: Ann Ford, with a guitar and a reputation to make
caption:
Ford was a performer, and this full-length portrait put her talent on show. Gainsborough was building his practice in Bath, so the picture advertised him too. She sits cross-legged with her guitar, an unusually relaxed pose for a formal portrait.

Image: Thomas Gainsborough, Portrait of Ann Ford, 1760. Cincinnati Art Museum. Public domain.

#gainsborough #guitar #womeninmusic #arthistory #musichistory

title: Pauline Viardot, posed as the patron saint of music
caption:
Pauline Viardot came from the García singing family and was a star across Europe. Saint-Saëns dedicated Samson and Delilah to her, and Brahms persuaded her to sing his Alto Rhapsody at its premiere. Ary Scheffer painted her as Saint Cecilia, the patron saint of music.

Image: Ary Scheffer, Pauline Viardot as Saint Cecilia. Musée de la Vie romantique, Paris. CC0.

#paulineviardot #womeninmusic #opera #arthistory #musichistory

title: Tchaikovsky's year at the piano: twelve months, twelve pieces
caption:
Every month gets its own piece, and the title page lists them all, from 'Janvier: Au coin du feu', by the fireside, to 'Décembre: La fête de Noël'. J. Hamelle published this Paris edition in 1903. Look at the little price table: you could buy one month at a time.

Image: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, Les Saisons, Op. 37 (title page, J. Hamelle edition), 1903. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#tchaikovsky #theseasons #pianomusic #sheetmusic #winter

title: Leonardo's only known portrait of a man
audio_search: Josquin des Prez, Missa Pange lingua
caption:
Leonardo finished the face and hair and left the rest. Look at his right hand: it holds a folded sheet of music, hidden under overpaint until a restoration in 1904 and 1905. The partly legible words may read Cantum Angelicum, angelic song.

Image: Leonardo da Vinci, Portrait of a Musician, c. 1483-87. Pinacoteca Ambrosiana, Milan. Public domain.

#leonardodavinci #renaissance #portrait #arthistory #musichistory

title: A Boston piano with drawers, 1814
caption:
American square pianos were household furniture, and this one even has storage. Look for the cornucopias on the nameboard. It predates Alpheus Babcock's 1825 patent for a one-piece iron frame, an idea that shaped the modern piano.

Image: Babcock, Appleton and Babcock, Square Piano, 1814. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#piano #squarepiano #boston #americanart #musichistory

title: Beethoven, copying out Mozart's Don Giovanni
audio_search: Mozart, Piano Sonata in C, K. 330, finale
caption:
Mozart's opera premiered in Prague on October 29, 1787. Here Beethoven wrote out bars 558 to 581 of the voice parts, and in two bars he swapped the lines of Don Giovanni and Leporello. Later pages of the same copy are in Berlin and Paris.

Image: Ludwig van Beethoven (copyist), Mozart, Don Giovanni, K. 527, Act 1 finale, fragment, c. 1815. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#beethoven #mozart #dongiovanni #opera #musichistory

title: Bach holds out a puzzle canon to the viewer
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Prelude No. 1 in C, BWV 846
caption:
Bach presented the portrait when he joined Lorenz Mizler's learned society of musicians in 1747, and the canon was his calling card. A copy made in 1748 belonged to his son Carl Philipp Emanuel. Look at the little sheet of music in his hand.

Image: Elias Gottlob Haussmann, Johann Sebastian Bach, 1746. Stadtgeschichtliches Museum Leipzig. Public domain.

#bach #composer #canon #baroque #arthistory #musichistory

title: Berlioz never studied piano. He played flute and guitar
audio_search: Berlioz, Les nuits d'été: Le spectre de la rose
caption:
Hector Berlioz wrote some of the boldest orchestral music of his century without being a pianist. Courbet shows only his head, lit from the side and floating in darkness, eyes cast down.

Image: Gustave Courbet, The Composer Hector Berlioz. Study, c. 1850. Nasjonalmuseet, Oslo. Public domain.

#berlioz #courbet #realism #arthistory #musichistory

title: The Stars and Stripes Forever, first edition, 1897
audio_search: Harry Austin Tierney, Black Canary Rag (1911)
caption:
John Philip Sousa composed The Stars and Stripes Forever in 1896, and it was published in 1897. Congress made it the official National March in 1987. This first page is from a copy in the Library of Congress.

Image: John Philip Sousa, The Stars and Stripes Forever, 1897. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#sousa #starsandstripesforever #march #sheetmusic #americanmusic

title: Chopin, painted by his friend Delacroix
audio_search: Chopin, Nocturne in E-flat, Op. 9 No. 2
caption:
Delacroix planned Chopin at the piano with George Sand listening, and even had a piano brought to his studio. The piano was never painted. After his death the canvas was cut apart, and Sand's half went to Copenhagen. Look at how loosely the face and hands are brushed, as if the music were still moving.

Image: Eugène Delacroix, Portrait of Frédéric Chopin, 1838. Musée du Louvre. Public domain.

#chopin #delacroix #romanticism #arthistory #musichistory #piano

title: The only surviving 11-course swan-neck lute
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Fugue No. 5, Well-Tempered Clavier Book 1
caption:
The back is built from 21 ribs of snakewood. A swan neck bends back to hold the bass strings. According to the museum, no other 11-course lute of this kind is known.

Image: Pietro Railich, Lute, 1669, altered by Anton Fichtl, 1720. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#lute #baroque #earlymusic #instruments #musichistory

title: A Mass from Antwerp, made as a gift for a pope
caption:
Barbireau led the choir of the Church of Our Lady in Antwerp from 1484; he died in 1491. This Mass divides some parts, so it needs at least ten singers. Look for the coat of arms of Leo X in the middle of the right-hand page.

Image: Jacques Barbireau, Missa Virgo parens Christi, Kyrie, early 16th-century copy. Vatican Library (Capp. Sist. 160). Public domain.

#barbireau #renaissancemusic #choirbook #musichistory #antwerp

title: Gluck at the keyboard, caught in the act of composing
audio_search: Beethoven, Moonlight Sonata, Op. 27 No. 2, first movement
caption:
Duplessis seated Gluck at a spinet, turning a working moment into a public image. The portrait now hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.

Image: Joseph Siffred Duplessis, Christoph Willibald Gluck, 1775. Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna. Public domain.

#gluck #composer #portrait #arthistory #musichistory

title: Mary Cassatt's banjo lesson, in color
caption:
Cassatt, an American working in Paris, made prints as carefully as paintings, often of quiet moments shared by women and girls. This one turns a music lesson into a study of closeness.

Image: Mary Cassatt, The Banjo Lesson, c. 1893. National Gallery of Art, Washington. CC0.

#marycassatt #banjo #printmaking #arthistory #womeninart

title: Ravel's Pavane, as his first publisher printed it
audio_search: Ravel, Le tombeau de Couperin: Toccata
caption:
Ravel was still a student of Fauré when he wrote this piano piece in 1899. He made an orchestral version in 1910. This color cover is from the edition published by E. Demets in Paris.

Image: Maurice Ravel, Pavane pour une infante défunte (E. Demets edition cover), c. 1900. Public domain.

#ravel #pavane #sheetmusic #pianomusic #frenchmusic

title: Gold cranes on a 17th-century Japanese koto
caption:
The koto is a long zither with 13 strings over movable bridges. The Goto family were master metalworkers. Its early 19th-century lacquer case is decorated with cranes and geese.

Image: Goto Teijo (metalwork), Koto, early 17th century. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#koto #japaneseart #instruments #musichistory #asianart

title: The Concert, or a concert interrupted?
caption:
Three men share one musical moment, and the keyboard player at the center turns away from his instrument toward the man behind him. Something has just stopped the music. A copy in Rome's Borghese Gallery adds a fourth figure.

Image: Titian, The Concert, c. 1510-11. Galleria Palatina, Palazzo Pitti, Florence. Public domain.

#titian #renaissance #venice #arthistory #musichistory

title: Chant without staff lines, St. Gallen, around 922
caption:
A monk at the abbey of St. Gallen wrote out the soloist's chants of the Mass between about 922 and 926. There are no staff lines: small neumes above the words show how the melody moves.

Image: Anonymous scribe, Cantatorium (Cod. Sang. 359), Introit and Gradual, c. 922-926. Abbey Library of St. Gallen. Public domain.

#gregorianchant #medievalmusic #manuscript #musichistory #neumes

title: A king plays flute while C. P. E. Bach looks bored
audio_search: Beethoven, Moonlight Sonata, Op. 27 No. 2, finale
caption:
Frederick the Great was a keen flutist, and here he plays for his court by candlelight. His teacher Quantz stands at the far right. At the harpsichord sits Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach, J. S. Bach's son, eyelids half closed. Look at the glow of the candles on the gilded walls.

Image: Adolph Menzel, Flute Concert of Frederick the Great at Sanssouci, 1850–52. Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin. Public domain.

#cpebach #flute #frederickthegreat #arthistory #musichistory #harpsichord

title: A serpent painted to look like a real snake
caption:
The serpent was a bass wind instrument played with a cup mouthpiece. In France it supported plainsong in church from the late 1500s. Handel, Haydn, Berlioz and Mendelssohn all wrote for it.

Image: C. Baudouin, Serpent, c. 1820. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#serpent #instruments #earlymusic #musichistory #paris

title: Dvořák gives his Ninth Symphony a name: From the New World
audio_search: Dvořák, Symphony No. 9 'From the New World', first movement
caption:
Dvořák spent 1892 to 1895 in America as director of the National Conservatory of Music. The Symphony No. 9 in E minor, Op. 95 was the result, and it became one of the most popular symphonies ever written. This is the title page of his autograph score.

Image: Antonín Dvořák, Symphony No. 9 in E minor, Op. 95 (title page of the autograph score), 1893. Public domain.

#dvorak #newworldsymphony #manuscript #classicalmusic #symphony

title: Music made with a helmet and two spoons
audio_search: Palestrina, Missa Papae Marcelli: Agnus Dei I
caption:
This is street music made from whatever was at hand. The helmet is an old morion, a soldier's helmet now drafted into the band. Ask your students what they could play from the kitchen drawer.

Image: Jan Miense Molenaer, Two Boys and a Girl Making Music, 1629. National Gallery, London. Public domain.

#janmiensemolenaer #children #dutchgoldenage #arthistory #musichistory

title: Beethoven in his thirties, with a lyre at his side
caption:
This is one of the few portraits of Beethoven as a young man. He sits in a landscape with a lyre-shaped instrument and lifts one hand, as if keeping time. Look for the small round temple among the trees at the left.

Image: Joseph Willibrord Mähler, Portrait of Beethoven, c. 1804–05. Wien Museum, Vienna. Public domain.

#beethoven #portrait #vienna #arthistory #musichistory

title: A page of Beethoven's Ninth, in his own hand
caption:
Beethoven finished the autograph in February 1824, and the premiere followed in Vienna on May 7. By most accounts the contralto Caroline Unger turned him around to see the applause. The score is in the Berlin State Library.

Image: Ludwig van Beethoven, Symphony No. 9 in D minor, Op. 125, autograph, page 12, 1822-1824. Berlin State Library. Public domain.

#beethoven #ninthsymphony #symphony #classicalmusic #musichistory

title: Rossetti lent his own violin to this painting
caption:
Rossetti painted Alexa Wilding as a musician catching a melody from a bird. The violin was his own. The quotation on the frame claims to come from an old Italian letter, but was probably written by Rossetti or Swinburne. Look for the bird and its open cage.

Image: Dante Gabriel Rossetti, Veronica Veronese, 1872. Delaware Art Museum. Public domain.

#rossetti #preraphaelite #violin #arthistory #musichistory

title: Two keyboards in one box. Antwerp, 1581
caption:
Hans Ruckers signed it in Latin: HANS RVCKERS ME FECIT. The lid motto reads MVSICA DVLCE LABORVM LEVAMEN, roughly 'music, sweet comfort for toil.' The painted lid shows a garden party with dining, music and kolf, an early relative of golf, beside a moated castle.

Image: Hans Ruckers the Elder, Double Virginal, 1581. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#harpsichord #virginal #ruckers #musichistory #earlymusic

title: Where Schubert's 'Unfinished' Symphony stops
caption:
In 1823 he sent the score to his friend Anselm Hüttenbrenner, who kept it hidden for decades. Johann von Herbeck conducted the premiere in Vienna on December 17, 1865. This facsimile of the third movement was printed in 1885 in a biography of Herbeck.

Image: Franz Schubert, Symphony No. 8 in B minor, D. 759, third movement, facsimile, 1885. From the biography of Johann von Herbeck by J. R. von Herbeck. Public domain.

#schubert #unfinishedsymphony #symphony #classicalmusic #musichistory

title: Lavinia Fontana painted herself from a mirror
caption:
This was Fontana's way of introducing herself: skilled, educated and musical. A Latin inscription says she painted it from a mirror. Look for the servant standing behind her.

Image: Lavinia Fontana, Self-Portrait at the Virginal with a Servant, 1577. Accademia Nazionale di San Luca, Rome. Public domain.

#laviniafontana #womeninart #virginal #renaissance #arthistory #musichistory

title: Brahms at the piano, sketched from life
audio_search: Brahms, Intermezzo in A major, Op. 118 No. 2
caption:
Beckerath shows the older Brahms at a grand piano, perched on a small red stool. Look at the cigar smoke curling up while he plays, eyes closed.

Image: Willy von Beckerath, Brahms at the Piano, 1896. Private collection. Public domain.

#brahms #piano #arthistory #musichistory #romanticism

title: Pauline Viardot turns Brahms's Hungarian Dances into a duet
caption:
Brahms's 21 Hungarian Dances were his most profitable works, and everyone arranged them. This version, for two voices, is 'arrangé par Mme Pauline Viardot', with French words by Victor Wilder. The duet opens 'Ah! plus vagabondes que les chèvres', more wandering than goats.

Image: Pauline Viardot after Johannes Brahms, Les Bohémiennes (J. Hamelle edition), 1898. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#paulineviardot #brahms #hungariandances #womencomposers #sheetmusic

title: Asian musicians with European instruments, Paris, 1754
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Fugue No. 7, Well-Tempered Clavier Book 1
caption:
Built in Paris in 1754 with two keyboards, it was later converted into a piano. Look for the maker's name, IOANNES GOERMANS, around the rose. Many French harpsichords did not survive the Revolution, which makes this one rarer still.

Image: Jean Goermans, Harpsichord converted to a piano, 1754. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#harpsichord #chinoiserie #couperin #musichistory #arthistory

title: Why is he called the hurdy-gurdy player with a fly?
audio_search: Scarlatti, Sonata in G major, K. 455
caption:
In French the painting is nicknamed the vielleur à la mouche, the hurdy-gurdy player with a fly. Look closely and you may spot the insect. La Tour painted his street musicians without flattery, every wrinkle and patch in place.

Image: Georges de La Tour, The Hurdy-Gurdy Player, c. 1620-25. Musée d'Arts de Nantes. Public domain.

#georgesdelatour #hurdygurdy #baroque #arthistory #musichistory

title: A king's theme, worked into a six-voice fugue
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Chaconne from Partita No. 2 in D minor, BWV 1004
caption:
Back in Leipzig, Bach wrote out the 'Thema Regium' and published the Musical Offering that September. One inscription, 'Regis Iussu Cantio Et Reliqua Canonica Arte Resoluta', has initials that spell 'ricercar'. This manuscript page is in the Berlin State Library.

Image: Johann Sebastian Bach, Musical Offering, BWV 1079, Ricercar a 6, autograph, 1747. Berlin State Library. Public domain.

#bach #musicaloffering #fugue #baroquemusic #musichistory

title: Van Gogh painted the doctor's daughter at the piano
caption:
Van Gogh wrote to his brother Theo that he had started this portrait in late June 1890, after two sketches. He gave it to her father, Dr. Gachet. Look at the tall, narrow format, unusual for him.

Image: Vincent van Gogh, Marguerite Gachet at the Piano, 1890. Kunstmuseum Basel. Public domain.

#vangogh #piano #postimpressionism #arthistory #musichistory

title: Clara Schumann and Joseph Joachim, in concert in 1854
caption:
Menzel sketched the pianist Clara Schumann and the young violinist Joseph Joachim playing together. Only a photograph of the pastel survives. Look at the lower left for Menzel's note, 'zur Erinnerung', in remembrance.

Image: Adolph Menzel, Joseph Joachim and Clara Schumann, 1854. Lost; reproduction via Deutsche Fotothek. Public domain.

#claraschumann #joachim #menzel #womeninmusic #arthistory #musichistory

title: Satie's Flabby Preludes (for a Dog), in his own neat hand
caption:
Satie's piano pieces from these years carry joke titles and dry instructions to the player. The first prelude, 'Voix d'intérieur', fits on a single page, and Satie dated it 11 juillet 1912 in the corner. His name is lettered across the top.

Image: Erik Satie, Préludes flasques (pour un chien) (autograph, first page), 1912. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#eriksatie #manuscript #pianomusic #frenchmusic #satie

title: A viol that became a cello, then a viol again
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Italian Concerto, first movement
caption:
Smaller bass viols like this were used for 'divisions', fast variations over a repeating bass. Look for the fingerboard decorated with foliage and birds. George Saint George restored it in 1899.

Image: Attributed to Barak Norman, Bass Viola da Gamba (Division Viol), 1692. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#viol #violadagamba #baroque #earlymusic #musichistory

title: The still life that got her into the Académie
caption:
She won her place with a still life of musical instruments, one of two reception pieces. Marie Antoinette later became her patron. Spend a moment on the textures: wood, strings, paper and cloth.

Image: Anne Vallayer-Coster, The Attributes of Music, 1770. Musée du Louvre, Paris. Public domain.

#annevallayercoster #womeninart #stilllife #instruments #arthistory #musichistory

title: Beethoven's last piano sonata starts here
audio_search: Beethoven, String Quartet Op. 18 No. 6, Scherzo
caption:
Beethoven dedicated it to Archduke Rudolf, his pupil and patron. Asked why there was no third movement, he supposedly said he had no time, though the story comes from the unreliable Anton Schindler. This is the first page of his autograph.

Image: Ludwig van Beethoven, Piano Sonata No. 32 in C minor, Op. 111, autograph, first page, 1822. Beethoven-Haus Bonn. Public domain.

#beethoven #pianosonata #piano #classicalmusic #musichistory

title: An angel bows a viol for the newborn
audio_search: Praetorius, Es ist ein Ros entsprungen
caption:
The monks of St. Anthony at Isenheim cared for the sick, and this altarpiece was made for them. In the center, a kneeling angel plays a bowed string instrument while other angels gather in a glowing chapel. To the right, Mary holds the child.

Image: Matthias Grünewald, Isenheim Altarpiece (Concert of Angels and Nativity), 1512 to 1516. Musée Unterlinden, Colmar. Public domain.

#christmas #grunewald #angels #arthistory #musichistory

title: She played for Lincoln at the White House as a child
caption:
Carreño was a pianist, singer and composer. Her little waltz for her daughter, Mi Teresita, became a favorite encore. This Bain photograph is undated but earlier than her death in 1917.

Image: Bain News Service, Teresa Carreño at the piano, before 1917. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#carreno #piano #womeninmusic #venezuela #musichistory

title: The best-selling song of the 1890s, and the face that sold it
audio_search: Harry Austin Tierney, Black Canary Rag (1911)
caption:
In this waltz song an old man explains why he never married: he saw his sweetheart kiss another man and wouldn't listen. Years later he learned it was her brother. The cover shows J. Aldrich Libbey, the singer who launched the song.

Image: Charles K. Harris, After the Ball (sheet music cover), 1892. New York Public Library. Public domain.

#tinpanalley #sheetmusic #waltz #aftertheball #1890s

title: Domenico Scarlatti, dressed as a knight
audio_search: Scarlatti, Sonata in D minor, K. 32
caption:
Scarlatti wrote 555 keyboard sonatas, many of them for his royal pupil Maria Barbara. He was born in Naples on October 26, 1685, the same year as Bach and Handel. His sonatas are still teaching staples.

Image: Domingo Antonio Velasco, Portrait of Domenico Scarlatti, 1738. Casa dos Patudos, Alpiarça. Public domain.

#scarlatti #harpsichord #composer #baroque #arthistory #musichistory

title: Rossetti's Christmas carol, sung in gold and holly
audio_search: Mendelssohn, Hark! The Herald Angels Sing
caption:
Rossetti fixed a short text to the frame describing a richly dressed maid singing of Christ's birth to an old carol melody. Look at the holly berries tied to the head of the instrument and her fingers on the strings. It was his second picture with this title, after a watercolor of 1857 to 1858.

Image: Dante Gabriel Rossetti, A Christmas Carol, 1867. Private collection. Public domain.

#christmas #rossetti #preraphaelite #arthistory #musichistory

title: One melody, sung at two speeds at once
audio_search: Palestrina, Missa Papae Marcelli: Agnus Dei II
caption:
Only one voice of each canon is written out, with mensuration signs that tell the singers how to read it. This copy is in the Chigi Codex, made for Philip I of Castile between 1498 and 1503, shortly after Ockeghem's death. It is now in the Vatican Library.

Image: Johannes Ockeghem, Missa prolationum, Kyrie, Chigi Codex, 1498-1503. Vatican Library (Chigi C. VIII. 234). Public domain.

#ockeghem #renaissancemusic #canon #musichistory #manuscript

title: Thomas Eakins painted his own sisters at home
caption:
Eakins painted this around 1871. It shows a mood more than a story: practice paused, homework underway. Look at how the piano fills the dark room.

Image: Thomas Eakins, Home Scene, c. 1871. Brooklyn Museum. Public domain.

#eakins #americanart #piano #arthistory #musichistory #practice

title: An 18th-century sitar from Rajasthan
caption:
A sitar has six or seven playing strings over curved, movable frets, plus many sympathetic strings that ring along. Look for the round gourd at the base. At over a meter long, it is an early survivor of the instrument.

Image: Indian maker, Sitar, 18th century. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#sitar #indianart #instruments #musichistory #asianart

title: Silent Night, written out by the man who composed it
caption:
Gruber was a schoolteacher and church organist when he set Joseph Mohr's poem in 1818. This copy, from around 1860, is one of his later autographs. It now belongs to the Stille-Nacht-Gesellschaft in Austria.

Image: Franz Xaver Gruber, Stille Nacht (autograph, version VII), c. 1860. Stille-Nacht-Gesellschaft. Public domain.

#silentnight #stillenacht #manuscript #christmasmusic #gruber

title: A family portrait, and everyone has an instrument
caption:
The Cleveland Museum of Art points out the luxuries on display: a Transylvanian rug, Chinese vases and Japanese lacquer. Music, like the imported treasures, said this was a cultured home. Look past the players to the objects around them.

Image: Pieter de Hooch, Portrait of a Family Playing Music, 1663. Cleveland Museum of Art. Public domain.

#pieterdehooch #familymusic #dutchgoldenage #arthistory #musichistory

title: Five angels, and the band starts playing
caption:
The angels stand beside the newborn Christ and perform for him, strings and voices together. Past restorations were heavy-handed, which is why some passages look thin or unfinished. Look for the two lutes among the singers.

Image: Piero della Francesca, The Nativity, c. 1470-75. National Gallery, London. Public domain.

#pierodellafrancesca #christmas #angels #lute #arthistory #musichistory

title: Jingle Bells, before it was called Jingle Bells
audio_search: Mendelssohn, Hark! The Herald Angels Sing
caption:
Pierpont's song was printed in Boston in 1857 under the title The One Horse Open Sleigh. It only became tied to winter and Christmas in the 1860s and 1870s. This is the first page of that 1857 edition from the Library of Congress.

Image: James Lord Pierpont, The One Horse Open Sleigh, 1857. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#jinglebells #sheetmusic #christmasmusic #americanmusic #1857

title: The first word sung at Christmas Mass, painted in gold
caption:
This leaf comes from a giant choirbook illuminated by Don Silvestro dei Gherarducci for the abbot of San Michele a Murano. Inside the P is the Nativity. At the bottom of the page a shepherd plays the bagpipe as an angel brings the news.

Image: Don Silvestro dei Gherarducci, Nativity in an initial P, leaf from a Gradual, c. 1392 to 1399. The Morgan Library & Museum. Public domain.

#christmas #gregorianchant #manuscript #medievalart #musichistory

title: The red scarf that made a cabaret singer famous
audio_search: Brahms, Capriccio in B minor, Op. 76 No. 2
caption:
Aristide Bruant sang rough, funny songs of Paris street life and ran his own cabaret, Le Mirliton. When he moved to the Café des Ambassadeurs in 1892, Lautrec made this poster. Look for the black cape and the famous red scarf, all flat, bold shapes.

Image: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, Ambassadeurs: Aristide Bruant, 1892. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#toulouselautrec #cabaret #poster #arthistory #musichistory

title: The first page of Bach's Mass in B minor
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Fugue No. 2 in C minor, BWV 847
caption:
Augustus III received the music on July 27, 1733. Bach later completed the Mass, BWV 232, and the earliest documented complete performance came in 1859. The autograph score is in the Berlin State Library.

Image: Johann Sebastian Bach, Mass in B minor, BWV 232, Kyrie, autograph, c. 1733-1749. Berlin State Library. Public domain.

#bach #massinbminor #baroquemusic #choir #musichistory

title: Tortoiseshell and ivory on a Hamburg guitar
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Prelude No. 5, Well-Tempered Clavier Book 1
caption:
Tielke was famous for lavishly decorated instruments. Look for the striped back in ebony and ivory. It was built with five pairs of strings and later converted to six single strings, like a modern guitar.

Image: Joachim Tielke, Guitar, c. 1695–99. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#guitar #baroque #tielke #earlymusic #musichistory

title: She taught herself to write a symphony
caption:
Beach's only formal composition lessons were in harmony and counterpoint, in 1881 and 1882. The rest she learned from books, even translating French treatises on orchestration. She made her concert debut as a pianist at 16.

Image: Bain News Service, Amy Marcy Cheney Beach, undated. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#amybeach #womeninmusic #composer #americanmusic #musichistory

title: Amy Beach's song in an animal-welfare magazine, Boston, 1893
caption:
The page credits the song to 'Mrs. H. H. A. Beach', the name she published under. The column below brags that 'Mrs. Dr. Beach, of Commonwealth Avenue, Boston' had written 'the first Mass ever written by a woman'. Beach was the first successful American woman composer of large-scale art music.

Image: Amy Beach, Golden Gates, in Our Dumb Animals, vol. 25 no. 8, January 1893. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#amybeach #womencomposers #sheetmusic #americanmusic #artsong

title: A tiny painting that a German prince called his crown
caption:
Christian Ludwig of Mecklenburg paid about 1,500 thalers for it and boasted of the crown he had carried off from Holland, to the envy of rival collectors. Because of a family feud it was first sent to Barth before reaching Schwerin.

Image: Frans van Mieris the Elder, Lady at the Harpsichord, 1658. Staatliches Museum Schwerin. Public domain.

#fransvanmieris #harpsichord #dutchgoldenage #arthistory #musichistory

title: Burne-Jones's Love Song: music in a dreamlike dusk
caption:
Burne-Jones, a Pre-Raphaelite, painted music as a mood more than an event. He worked on this canvas on and off for nearly a decade.

Image: Edward Burne-Jones, The Love Song, 1868–77. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#burnejones #preraphaelite #metmuseum #arthistory #musichistory

title: Chopin's own manuscript of the Heroic Polonaise
caption:
Chopin composed this polonaise in 1842 and dedicated it to his friend, the banker Auguste Léo. His student Adolphe Gutmann said Chopin played it more gently than most pianists do. This page is in Chopin's own hand, and the manuscript now belongs to the Morgan Library & Museum in New York.

Image: Frédéric Chopin, Polonaise in A-flat major, Op. 53 (autograph manuscript), 1842. Morgan Library & Museum. Public domain.

#chopin #heroicpolonaise #manuscript #pianomusic #romanticera

title: Built in 1792, a year before Broadwood gave up harpsichords
audio_search: Haydn, Sonata in C minor, finale
caption:
Haydn and Beethoven both admired Broadwood's instruments. This one is mahogany with fine holly stringing and a curly maple nameboard. By 1793 the firm had moved entirely from harpsichords to pianos.

Image: John Broadwood, Grand Piano, 1792. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#piano #fortepiano #haydn #broadwood #musichistory

title: He found the Bach cello suites in a secondhand shop
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Fugue No. 2 in C minor, BWV 847
caption:
Casals was browsing a bundle of scores near the Barcelona harbor in 1890. The suites became central to his playing, and to every cellist since. Bain News Service photographed him in the 1910s or 1920s.

Image: Bain News Service, Pablo Casals, c. 1910s–20s. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#casals #cello #bach #musichistory #strings

title: Dedicated 'to the artists': Paganini's 24 Caprices, 1820
caption:
Instead of a patron, Paganini dedicated the set to the artists, 'agli artisti'. Caprice No. 24 in A minor later inspired Liszt, Brahms and Rachmaninoff. Look for the price at right: 9 Italian lire.

Image: Niccolò Paganini, 24 Capricci per violino solo, Op. 1, first edition title page, Milan: Ricordi, 1820. Scan of a privately held copy. Public domain.

#paganini #violin #caprice #firstedition #musichistory

title: Angelica Kauffman had to choose: opera or painting?
audio_search: Haydn, 'Lark' Quartet, Op. 64 No. 5, first movement
caption:
As a young woman Kauffman was pulled between the opera stage and art, and a priest warned her the opera was full of 'seedy people.' She chose painting, and in 1768 became one of two women among the founders of the Royal Academy in London. Decades later she painted the moment of decision. Look at how she turns between the two figures.

Image: Angelica Kauffman, Self-Portrait Hesitating between the Arts of Music and Painting, 1794. Nostell Priory, National Trust. Public domain.

#angelicakauffman #womeninart #neoclassical #arthistory #musichistory

title: Eakins carved the music into the frame
caption:
Weda Cook sang an aria from Mendelssohn's Elijah during the sittings so Eakins could watch her throat and mouth. Look at the lower left corner for a conductor's hand and baton, and the bouquet at her feet that hints at an encore.

Image: Thomas Eakins, The Concert Singer, 1890–92. Philadelphia Museum of Art. Public domain.

#eakins #singer #americanart #arthistory #musichistory

title: The first page of Scheherazade, in manuscript full score
caption:
The page opens 'Largo e maestoso' with the stern theme of the Sultan, heard in the low brass and strings. Every instrument has its own line, from piccolo at the top down through the harp to the double basses. The work is famous for its dazzling orchestration.

Image: Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov, Scheherazade, Op. 35 (first page of the manuscript full score), c. 1888. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#rimskykorsakov #scheherazade #manuscript #orchestra #russianmusic

title: Caruso, with the machine that made him famous
audio_search: Brahms, Intermezzo in B-flat, Op. 117 No. 2
caption:
Caruso was one of the first singers whose fame grew from records as much as from the stage. His first recordings were cut in Milan in 1902. Here, around 1913, he poses beside a Victrola.

Image: Bain News Service, Enrico Caruso with Victrola, c. 1913. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#caruso #opera #phonograph #musichistory #recording

title: A koto, wrapped and waiting for the New Year
caption:
Surimono were privately commissioned prints that paired pictures with poems, often as New Year greetings. Here Hokusai lays out a koto in its protective cover, a bamboo flute and a little table of New Year offerings. The shell in the fan-shaped panel gives the print its title.

Image: Katsushika Hokusai, Akoya Shell (Genroku Poem-Shell Contest), 1821. Rijksmuseum. Public domain.

#hokusai #koto #surimono #newyear #japaneseart

title: Beethoven's New Year canon, dated the last day of 1819
audio_search: Beethoven, Piano Concerto No. 4, first movement
caption:
Look at the date at bottom right. Beethoven first wrote 1820, then corrected it to 1819. The words pass from voice to voice, each singer wishing luck for the year ahead.

Image: Ludwig van Beethoven, Glück, Glück zum neuen Jahr!, WoO 176, autograph, December 31, 1819. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#beethoven #newyear #canon #choir #musichistory

title: A lute with a broken string, hidden in plain sight
caption:
Two French envoys stand beside shelves crowded with the learning of their age. On the lower shelf, look for the lute: one string has snapped, a sign of discord. Next to it a hymnbook lies open, and the case of flutes seems to be missing one. The smear across the floor is a skull, readable only from the side.

Image: Hans Holbein the Younger, The Ambassadors, 1533. National Gallery, London. Public domain.

#holbein #lute #renaissance #arthistory #musichistory

title: The English Bach, painted by his friend Gainsborough
audio_search: Mozart, Piano Sonata in C, K. 330, first movement
caption:
Bach first asked Gainsborough to paint him for Giovanni Battista Martini's gallery of musicians in Bologna, then ordered this second version for himself. In London he met the young Mozart in 1764 and became a key influence. He also ran the Bach-Abel concerts, an early model of the public concert series.

Image: Thomas Gainsborough, Johann Christian Bach, 1776. National Portrait Gallery, London. Public domain.

#jcbach #gainsborough #composer #portrait #arthistory #musichistory

title: Trifles for a piano method, dated New Year's Day 1821
caption:
This is the last leaf of the manuscript. At right, in 1858, the Vienna choirmaster Carl Pichler wrote a note vouching for the handwriting and giving the date of composition as January 1, 1821. The five pieces were published that June.

Image: Ludwig van Beethoven, Kleinigkeiten (Bagatelles Op. 119 Nos. 7-11), autograph, last leaf, 1820-1821. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#beethoven #bagatelles #piano #classicalmusic #musichistory

title: The Waltz King conducts a Vienna court ball
audio_search: Johann Strauss II, The Blue Danube
caption:
Until 1870, Strauss played the annual court balls, family balls and children's balls of the Habsburg court. For family balls in the imperial apartments, the band shrank to about ten players. Look for Strauss at the front, leading with his violin.

Image: Theo Zasche, Johann Strauss II and his orchestra at a court ball, c. 1890. Wien Museum. Public domain.

#johannstrauss #waltz #vienna #newyear #musichistory

title: Henry Ossawa Tanner's Banjo Lesson
audio_search: Brahms, Intermezzo in B-flat, Op. 117 No. 2
caption:
Tanner, who had studied with Thomas Eakins, painted this in 1893 to show a tender, serious lesson. The boy holds a chord with one hand and plucks with the other. Look at the two lights: cool from the window, warm from the fire.

Image: Henry Ossawa Tanner, The Banjo Lesson, 1893. Hampton University Museum. Public domain.

#henryossawatanner #banjo #americanart #arthistory #musichistory #musiclesson

title: Handel writes music for a coronation, 1727
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Italian Concerto, Andante
caption:
Handel became a naturalized British subject the same year. Of the four anthems, Zadok the Priest has been sung at every British coronation since. This page of The King Shall Rejoice is in Handel's own hand.

Image: George Frideric Handel, The King Shall Rejoice, HWV 260, autograph, f. 16r, 1727. British Library (Add MS 30308). Public domain.

#handel #coronation #baroquemusic #choir #musichistory

title: The March King called records 'canned music'
caption:
Sousa led the U.S. Marine Band from 1880 to 1892 and wrote The Stars and Stripes Forever in 1896. The sousaphone was built for him by J. W. Pepper. Frances Benjamin Johnston, a pioneering woman photographer, took this portrait in 1904.

Image: Frances Benjamin Johnston, John Philip Sousa, 1904. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#sousa #marches #band #musichistory #americanmusic

title: Memling's angel orchestra, made for a Spanish church
caption:
Three panels survive, filled with angels who sing and play wind and string instruments around Christ. They now hang in Antwerp. Pick one angel and follow the instrument from mouthpiece to bell.

Image: Hans Memling, Music-making Angels, 1483-94. Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA). Public domain.

#memling #angels #earlymusic #flemishart #arthistory #musichistory

title: Grieg's first title for Wedding Day at Troldhaugen
audio_search: Brahms, Intermezzo in E-flat minor, Op. 118 No. 6
caption:
At the top of his manuscript, Grieg's first title seems to read 'Die Gratulanten kommen', the well-wishers are coming. The piece opens 'Tempo di Marcia' in D major. Troldhaugen was Grieg's home near Bergen, and this page belongs to the Grieg collection of the Bergen Public Library.

Image: Edvard Grieg, Wedding Day at Troldhaugen, Op. 65 No. 6 (autograph, first page), 1896. Bergen Public Library, Grieg Archives. Public domain.

#grieg #lyricpieces #manuscript #pianomusic #norway

title: Sargent's flamenco painting is almost 12 feet wide
caption:
Sargent toured Spain and North Africa for five months in 1879 and came back with this huge flamenco scene. Isabella Stewart Gardner later built her Spanish Cloister around it, framed by a Moorish arch.

Image: John Singer Sargent, El Jaleo, 1882. Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston. Public domain.

#sargent #flamenco #guitar #arthistory #musichistory

title: A square piano carved on every side
caption:
Nunns and Clark ran a factory in Setauket, New York, turning out about 300 instruments a year. A similar piano was shown in London in 1851. Look inside: even the iron frame is painted with birds and insects.

Image: Robert Nunns and John Clark, Square Piano, 1853. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#piano #squarepiano #americanart #musichistory #newyork

title: Sei Solo: Bach's six works for violin alone, 1720
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Chaconne from Partita No. 2 in D minor, BWV 1004
caption:
No bass line, no keyboard: one violin carries everything. The six works include the Second Partita, which ends with the famous Chaconne. The manuscript reached Berlin's Royal Library in 1917 and is now in the Berlin State Library.

Image: Johann Sebastian Bach, Sei Solo a Violino senza Basso accompagnato, BWV 1001-1006, autograph title page, 1720. Berlin State Library (Mus.ms. Bach P 967). Public domain.

#bach #violin #baroquemusic #chaconne #musichistory

title: An emperor plays the qin for his ministers
caption:
Under a pine, a man in a Daoist robe plays the qin, the seven-string zither of Chinese scholars, while two officials listen. The work is long credited to Huizong, who reigned 1100 to 1126, though scholars now think a court painter made it. Look for the incense burner and the silence the painter builds around the sound.

Image: Attributed to Emperor Huizong, Listening to the Qin, Northern Song dynasty, early 12th century. The Palace Museum, Beijing. Public domain.

#guqin #chineseart #songdynasty #arthistory #musichistory

title: Madame Jones, and every medal she was given
audio_search: Verdi, Luisa Miller: Quando le sere al placido
caption:
A critic nicknamed her the Black Patti, after the opera star Adelina Patti; she preferred Madame Jones. In 1892 she sang for about 75,000 people at Madison Square Garden. This 1899 poster shows her wearing her medals.

Image: Poster for Mme. M. Sissieretta Jones, The Black Patti, 1899. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#sissierettajones #blackhistory #opera #singer #musichistory

title: Holst's Planets, in its first printed full score
caption:
Holst named each of the seven movements after a planet and its astrological character. The first performance was at the Queen's Hall, London, on September 29, 1918, before an invited audience. This is the cover of the full score printed in 1921.

Image: Gustav Holst, The Planets, Op. 32 (full score cover), 1921. Imogen Holst collection. Public domain.

#holst #theplanets #sheetmusic #orchestra #britishmusic

title: A royal wedding party, with the orchestra up in the clouds
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Italian Concerto, Presto
caption:
Cardinal de La Rochefoucauld, France's ambassador in Rome, staged an opera by Leonardo Vinci for the occasion. Look up at the musicians, rows of them half hidden behind a painted cloud, with cellos and basses easiest to spot. Below, singers dressed as Olympian gods face cardinals seated on carpets.

Image: Giovanni Paolo Panini, Musical Feast Given by the Cardinal de La Rochefoucauld at the Teatro Argentina in Rome, 1747. Musée du Louvre, Paris. Public domain.

#panini #opera #rome #baroque #arthistory #musichistory

title: Repin's portrait of Mussorgsky, days before his death
audio_search: Brahms, Intermezzo in C-sharp minor, Op. 117 No. 3
caption:
Ilya Repin rushed to the hospital to paint his friend. He gave the money from the painting toward a monument for the composer. Look at the hospital dressing gown, the unkempt hair and the steady, distant eyes.

Image: Ilya Repin, Portrait of Modest Mussorgsky, 1881. State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow. Public domain.

#mussorgsky #repin #russianart #arthistory #musichistory

title: Pope Gregory, pictured dictating the chants
caption:
Hartker's antiphoner holds the chants the monks of St. Gallen sang at their daily hours of prayer. Its library calls it a masterpiece of script, neumes and illuminated initials. This drawing, on page 13 of the winter volume, shows Pope Gregory I dictating the chants.

Image: Hartker, Gregory the Great dictating, Hartker Antiphoner (Cod. Sang. 390, p. 13), c. 990-1000. Abbey Library of St. Gallen. Public domain.

#gregorianchant #medievalart #manuscript #musichistory #stgallen

title: A saxophone made by Mr. Sax himself
caption:
Orchestras were slow to welcome the saxophone, but military bands loved it from the start. Look for the maker's engraving on the bell. This is one of the earliest generation of saxophones.

Image: Adolphe Sax, Alto Saxophone in E-flat, c. 1855. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#saxophone #adolphesax #instruments #musichistory #woodwinds

title: Krishna's flute, and seven women in the band
caption:
Malar is a mode tied to the rainy season, and the sky here is dark with clouds and streaks of gold lightning. Krishna stands at the center of a white platform with his flute. Count the seven gopis and their instruments, then find the peacocks in the trees.

Image: Malar Ragini: Krishna Playing the Flute to Seven Gopis, Bundi-Kota, c. 1760. Cleveland Museum of Art. Public domain.

#ragamala #krishna #indianart #flute #musichistory

title: Clair de lune, as Paris first saw it in print, 1905
caption:
This is the first page of Clair de lune from the first edition. It opens pianissimo in D-flat major, marked 'Andante très expressif' and 'con sordina'. Debussy waited about fifteen years to publish the suite, and Clair de lune became one of the most famous piano pieces ever written.

Image: Claude Debussy, Suite bergamasque: Clair de lune, first edition (E. Fromont), 1905. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#debussy #clairdelune #suitebergamasque #pianomusic #firstedition

title: A family band, staging concerts on a Thames barge
audio_search: Minuet in G from the Anna Magdalena Notebook
caption:
The Sharp siblings held concerts aboard their barge on the Thames, and Zoffany fitted the whole family in, instruments and all. Look for All Saints Church, Fulham in the background. The painting was shown at the Royal Academy in 1781.

Image: Johann Zoffany, The Sharp Family, 1779-81. Private collection, on loan to the National Gallery, London. Public domain.

#zoffany #familymusic #georgian #arthistory #musichistory

title: The first American violinist with an international career
caption:
Born in Peru, Illinois, Powell studied with Joseph Joachim in Berlin. From 1904 she was among the first instrumentalists to make Red Seal records for Victor. She also commissioned a violin concerto from Samuel Coleridge-Taylor.

Image: Unknown photographer, Maud Powell, 1919. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#maudpowell #violin #womeninmusic #musichistory #americanmusic

title: 'Sonata quasi una fantasia', Vienna, 1802
audio_search: Beethoven, Moonlight Sonata, Op. 27 No. 2, first movement
caption:
Beethoven finished the sonata in 1801 and dedicated it to his pupil Countess Giulietta Guicciardi. The nickname traces back to a comparison by the critic Ludwig Rellstab in 1824, though no one knows when it caught on. This title page is from the Beethoven-Haus Bonn copy.

Image: Ludwig van Beethoven, Sonata quasi una fantasia, Op. 27 No. 2, first edition title page, Vienna: Cappi, 1802. Beethoven-Haus Bonn. Public domain.

#beethoven #moonlightsonata #piano #firstedition #musichistory

title: The Swedish Nightingale, painted in Berlin
caption:
Jenny Lind was the most famous singer of her day, nicknamed the Swedish Nightingale. In 1850 she sailed to America for a Barnum tour of 93 concerts. Look at the calm, direct face that sold out halls on two continents.

Image: Eduard Magnus, Jenny Lind. Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin. Public domain.

#jennylind #mendelssohn #opera #womeninmusic #arthistory #musichistory

title: Steinway's flagship, finished January 9, 1869
caption:
Steinway called the design 'Plain Grand Style 2'. The museum records that a craftsman named Hebeler finished the case, and the piano sold that year to a G. DeForest. Count the keys: 88, the number that became standard.

Image: Steinway & Sons, Grand Piano, 1868. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#steinway #piano #newyork #musichistory #gottschalk

title: Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition, dedicated to Stasov
audio_search: Brahms, Intermezzo in E-flat, Op. 117 No. 1
caption:
Each movement of Pictures at an Exhibition depicts a work by the painter and architect Viktor Hartmann. The title page carries Mussorgsky's dedication 'A Monsieur Wladimir Stasov'. This Bessel edition also notes 'Matériel d'orchestre en location', orchestral parts for hire, because by then Ravel's 1922 orchestration had made the suite famous.

Image: Modest Mussorgsky, Tableaux d'une exposition (title page, W. Bessel edition), 1925. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#mussorgsky #picturesatanexhibition #pianomusic #sheetmusic #russianmusic

title: Inside a royal piano factory, Copenhagen, 1913
audio_search: Brahms, Rhapsody in G minor, Op. 79 No. 2
caption:
Hornung built his first piano in 1827, and the firm became supplier to the Danish royal court in 1843. From 1872 it worked out of Dehns Palace on Bredgade, which doubled as a showroom. Elfelt was a Danish photographer and film director.

Image: Peter Elfelt, Hornung & Møller piano factory, 1913. Public domain.

#piano #pianofactory #copenhagen #denmark #musichistory

title: Two musicians at a 15-day Ottoman festival
caption:
This detail shows two women musicians, one with a long-necked lute and one with a frame drum fitted with jingles. Look at the painted fingernails on the drum and the flowers tucked into their headdresses.

Image: Levni, Surname-i Vehbi (detail of fol. 17b), 1720. Topkapı Palace Museum Library. Public domain.

#ottomanart #miniature #levni #arthistory #musichistory

title: 336 pieces of 13th-century polyphony in one book
caption:
Most of its pieces are motets. The biggest group are French songs of courtly love, alongside Latin and mixed-language motets. The book still lives in Montpellier, in the medical section of the university library.

Image: Anonymous, Montpellier Codex (H196), fol. 23v-24r, c. 1300. Bibliothèque Inter-Universitaire de Montpellier. Public domain.

#medievalmusic #motet #manuscript #musichistory #arsantiqua

title: She writes a song. He reads over her shoulder
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Prelude No. 7, Well-Tempered Clavier Book 1
caption:
The young woman is composing, pen in hand, while the man leans in to see what she has written. Behind them another woman keeps playing. Look up at the painting over the mantel: a ship caught in a storm.

Image: Gabriël Metsu, A Young Woman Composing a Piece of Music, c. 1664. Mauritshuis, The Hague. Public domain.

#gabrielmetsu #composer #dutchgoldenage #arthistory #musichistory

title: Carl Larsson at night: one lamp, one pianist
audio_search: Schubert, Sonata in A, D. 664, first movement
caption:
A tall, dark room with a balcony and big windows, and only one corner lit. Someone sits at the grand piano under the lamp. Look how far into the picture you have to go to find the musician.

Image: Carl Larsson, At the Piano (Vid flygeln), 1900. Thiel Gallery, Stockholm. Public domain.

#carllarsson #scandinavianart #piano #arthistory #musichistory

title: Orpheus in the Underworld, the show that gave us the can-can
audio_search: Brahms, Waltz in A-flat, Op. 39 No. 15
caption:
Offenbach's Orphée aux enfers turns the Greek myth upside down: Orpheus is a violin teacher who is glad to be rid of his wife. It opened in 1858, and the big four-act version followed at the Théâtre de la Gaîté in 1874. Jules Chéret, the father of the modern poster, printed this one. Look for 'Tous les soirs', every night, at the top left.

Image: Jules Chéret, poster for Jacques Offenbach's Orphée aux enfers at the Théâtre de la Gaîté, 1878. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#offenbach #cancan #operetta #poster #paris

title: The hidden back of a Ming pipa
audio_search: Ravel, Miroirs: Une barque sur l'océan
caption:
A pipa is played upright, facing the audience, so this decoration faced the player. The plaques show Taoist, Confucian and Buddhist figures. Look for the bats, a symbol of good fortune in China.

Image: Chinese maker, Pipa, Ming dynasty, late 16th–early 17th century. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#pipa #chineseart #mingdynasty #instruments #musichistory

title: Dinner music outside a royal tent, Herat style
caption:
It is the left half of a double page from the late Timurid world. Musicians in the upper left provide the soundtrack while servants carry food. Because it is unfinished, you can see how color was laid over the underdrawing.

Image: Style of Bihzad, Outside a Royal Encampment (left half of a double-page folio), c. 1485. Cleveland Museum of Art. CC0.

#persianart #miniature #bihzad #arthistory #musichistory

title: Mozart writes for the glass harmonica
audio_search: Mozart, String Quartet in D minor, K. 421, Andante
caption:
Kirchgessner lost her sight to smallpox at age four. Mozart wrote her two works: this Adagio and the Adagio and Rondo, K. 617. Look for the word 'Harmonica' at the head of the page.

Image: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Adagio in C major for glass harmonica, K. 356 (617a), autograph, 1791. Bibliothèque nationale de France (MS-220). Public domain.

#mozart #glassharmonica #classicalmusic #womeninmusic #musichistory

title: A royal family band that was not in harmony
caption:
Anne plays the harpsichord, a sister plucks a mandola, and another reads from Milton. The relaxed scene belies the family's dislike of Frederick. Behind them stands the Dutch House at Kew, where Anne lived before her marriage in 1734.

Image: Philippe Mercier, The Music Party: Frederick, Prince of Wales, and His Sisters, 1733. National Portrait Gallery, London. Public domain.

#mercier #cello #harpsichord #georgian #arthistory #musichistory

title: Paganini, as Delacroix saw him at the Paris Opera
caption:
Contemporaries found the violinist's looks strange, but on stage he was electrifying. Delacroix painted him the year he heard him play in Paris, small and dark, on cardboard.

Image: Eugène Delacroix, Paganini, 1831. The Phillips Collection, Washington. Public domain.

#paganini #delacroix #violin #arthistory #musichistory

title: Swans on the cover of Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake, Moscow edition
caption:
This is the cover of Jurgenson's piano score of Swan Lake, arranged by Nikolai Kashkin. Three swans glide across a lake framed by reeds, under the Russian title Lebedinoe ozero. A Paris label from Félix Mackar is pasted at the bottom.

Image: P. Jurgenson, Swan Lake by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, piano arrangement by Nikolai Kashkin (cover), c. 1877-95. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#tchaikovsky #swanlake #ballet #sheetmusic #russianmusic

title: Printed paper, painted flowers, Antwerp, 1622
audio_search: Scarlatti, Sonata in G major, K. 146
caption:
Ruckers instruments were dressed in block-printed papers, a cheaper look than carving. The motto asks that every breath praise the Lord: OMNIS SPIRITUS LAUDET DOMINUM. Look for the gilded rose in the soundboard with the maker's initials, IR. Its keyboard was later enlarged from 45 to 54 notes.

Image: Joannes Ruckers, Muselar Virginal, 1622. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#virginal #ruckers #harpsichord #earlymusic #musichistory

title: The poet called 'Praise of Ladies', with his band
audio_search: Palestrina, Missa Papae Marcelli: Agnus Dei I
caption:
The Codex Manesse collects German love songs with full-page pictures of their poets. Frauenlob's page is a whole concert: find the fiddler in the middle, plus pipes, a drum and more. Legend says the women of Mainz carried his coffin to the cathedral in 1318.

Image: Codex Manesse, Meister Heinrich Frauenlob (fol. 399r), Zurich, c. 1304 to 1340. Heidelberg University Library. Public domain.

#medievalart #minnesang #manuscript #codexmanesse #musichistory

title: Barbara Strozzi, Venice, 1659: Opus 7
caption:
Diporti di Euterpe, 'Euterpe's pastimes', is her Opus 7. The poet Giulio Strozzi, who called her his adoptive daughter, founded an academy that staged performances at their home. This copy is at the Library of Congress.

Image: Barbara Strozzi, Diporti di Euterpe, Op. 7, title page, 1659. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#barbarastrozzi #womencomposers #baroquemusic #musichistory #venice

title: Sofonisba Anguissola, at the keyboard in 1561
caption:
For a young woman of her time, music and painting were both marks of a fine education, and Anguissola showed off both at once. This picture belongs to the Spencer family collection at Althorp.

Image: Sofonisba Anguissola, Self-Portrait at the Clavichord, 1561. Althorp House, Spencer Collection. Public domain.

#sofonisbaanguissola #womeninart #clavichord #renaissance #arthistory #musichistory

title: Degas painted his father, listening hard
caption:
Auguste De Gas loved music and hosted Monday evening gatherings in his Paris music room. Here the tenor Lorenzo Pagans sings to his own guitar while the old man sits behind him, hands clasped. Look for the dark grand piano behind them, with sheet music piled on its closed lid.

Image: Edgar Degas, Lorenzo Pagans and Auguste De Gas, c. 1871–72. Musée d'Orsay, Paris. Public domain.

#degas #guitar #impressionism #arthistory #musichistory

title: Handy sold The Memphis Blues. This 1913 edition added words
audio_search: W. C. Handy, St. Louis Blues (1922 recording)
caption:
W. C. Handy put out The Memphis Blues as an instrumental in 1912 and sold the rights soon after, something he later complained about bitterly. Theron Bennett hired George A. Norton to add words. Under the title this page reads 'Founded on W. C. Handy's World Wide Blue Note Melody'.

Image: W. C. Handy (music), George A. Norton (words), The Memphis Blues, Theron C. Bennett, 1913. Public domain.

#wchandy #memphisblues #blues #sheetmusic #ragtime

title: The first woman composer in the Légion d'honneur
caption:
Chaminade was a pianist and composer whose salon pieces sold in huge numbers. As a girl she played her music for Georges Bizet, who was impressed. In 1908 she gave concerts in twelve American cities.

Image: Unknown photographer, Cécile Chaminade, 1913. Public domain.

#chaminade #womeninmusic #composer #piano #musichistory

title: A singer with a kithara, mid-song, 490 BCE
caption:
The kithara was the lyre used for public performance, including epic poetry. On the other side of this Athenian amphora stands a judge with his wand, so the scene is probably a competition. Look at the long robe and the instrument's heavy wooden arms.

Image: Attributed to the Berlin Painter, Terracotta amphora, c. 490 BCE. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#lyre #ancientgreece #greekvase #arthistory #musichistory

title: Bach's Prelude 'for lute or harpsichord'
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Prelude No. 15 in G major, BWV 860
caption:
The Prelude, Fugue and Allegro in E-flat major, BWV 998, leaves the instrument to the player: lute or harpsichord. This manuscript is in Bach's own hand. The sale price was 2,518,500 pounds.

Image: Johann Sebastian Bach, Prelude, Fugue and Allegro in E-flat major, BWV 998, autograph, c. 1735. Sold at Christie's, London, 2016. Public domain.

#bach #lute #harpsichord #baroquemusic #musichistory

title: Is she tuning up, or about to play?
caption:
Orazio, Artemisia's father, painted this around 1612 to 1620. The National Gallery of Art suggests she may be tuning the lute before the others join her. Count the instruments on the table, laid out for a whole ensemble.

Image: Orazio Gentileschi, The Lute Player, c. 1612/1620. National Gallery of Art, Washington. Public domain.

#oraziogentileschi #lute #baroque #arthistory #musichistory

title: The instrument Benjamin Franklin invented
audio_search: Mozart, String Quartet in D minor, K. 421, Andante
caption:
Franklin named it after Italian, 'armonica'. Mozart wrote his Adagio and Rondo, K. 617, and an Adagio, K. 356, for it in 1791. This example, possibly German, 18th century, came to the museum with the Crosby Brown collection in 1889.

Image: Possibly German maker, Glass Harmonica, 18th century. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#glassharmonica #franklin #mozart #instruments #musichistory

title: Fauré's Dolly Suite, written for a little girl's birthdays
audio_search: Fauré, Cantique de Jean Racine, Op. 11
caption:
Each piece in the Dolly Suite marked a birthday or other moment in the life of a young girl, the daughter of Emma Bardac. The Berceuse is the best known, and it has been arranged for all sorts of instruments. This is the title page of the J. Hamelle edition.

Image: Gabriel Fauré, Dolly, Op. 56 (J. Hamelle edition, title page), 1894. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#faure #dollysuite #pianoduet #sheetmusic #frenchmusic

title: Hush! A violinist waits for the room to go quiet
audio_search: Saint-Saëns, Caprice on Danish and Russian Airs, Op. 79
caption:
Tissot, a Frenchman in London, loved fashionable crowds and their small social dramas. The title says it all: the room must go quiet before the music can begin.

Image: James Tissot, Hush! (The Concert), c. 1875. Manchester Art Gallery. Public domain.

#tissot #violin #victorianart #arthistory #musichistory

title: The Wagner fans of Paris, gathered around a piano
caption:
Fantin-Latour painted eight music lovers around Emmanuel Chabrier, who spent 19 years as a government clerk before music won. The picture was nicknamed The Wagnerists. Its first owner said the score on the piano was by Brahms. Look for the friend in the top hat at the far left, and the one turning Chabrier's page.

Image: Henri Fantin-Latour, Around the Piano, 1885. Musée d'Orsay, Paris. Public domain.

#chabrier #wagner #fantinlatour #arthistory #musichistory #piano

title: Haydn's only London symphony in a minor key
caption:
It was first played in 1791 at the Hanover Square Rooms in London, with Haydn conducting. Listen for the trio of the minuet, a solo for the cello. This page is in Haydn's own hand.

Image: Joseph Haydn, Symphony No. 95 in C minor, Hob. I:95, autograph, f. 1v, 1791. British Library (Add MS 64935). Public domain.

#haydn #symphony #classicalmusic #cello #musichistory

title: From the concert stage to running a country
caption:
Paderewski served as Prime Minister and Foreign Minister in 1919 and signed the Treaty of Versailles for Poland. His Minuet in G, written in the style of Mozart, became one of the best-known piano tunes ever. This portrait dates from 1921.

Image: National Photo Company, Ignacy Paderewski, 1921. Public domain.

#paderewski #piano #poland #musichistory #pianist

title: 'The Antonius' Stradivari, made in 1711
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Fugue No. 9 in E major, BWV 854
caption:
Stradivari made it in his Cremona workshop in 1711. His flatter arching helped the sound carry. Look at the warm varnish and the elegant scroll. The museum notes that the old story of his training with Amati is doubted, based on census records.

Image: Antonio Stradivari, "The Antonius" Violin, 1711. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#violin #stradivari #cremona #musichistory #strings

title: The first page of Chopin's last ballade, in his hand
audio_search: Chopin, Ballade No. 4 in F minor, Op. 52
caption:
Chopin completed his fourth and final ballade in 1842 and dedicated it to Baroness Charlotte de Rothschild. It is the longest of the four, usually ten to twelve minutes. This autograph first page is held by the Bodleian Library in Oxford.

Image: Frédéric Chopin, Ballade No. 4 in F minor, Op. 52 (autograph, first page), 1842. Bodleian Library, Oxford. Public domain.

#chopin #ballade #manuscript #pianomusic #fminor

title: A biwa, dressed in brocade
caption:
This small surimono comes from a series devoted to musical instruments. The biwa lies in its patterned cloth case, the way a treasured instrument was stored. Look at the curve of the neck and the bent-back pegbox.

Image: Ryūryūkyo Shinsai, Biwa with Brocade Cover (series Musical Instruments), probably 1808. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#biwa #surimono #japaneseart #instruments #musichistory

title: A piano prodigy with more than 70 patents
audio_search: Chopin, Mazurka in C minor, Op. 30 No. 1
caption:
Hofmann was Anton Rubinstein's only private student. As an inventor he worked on car and airplane shock absorbers and even a windshield wiper. He later directed the Curtis Institute of Music, from 1927 to 1938.

Image: Unknown photographer, Josef Casimir Hofmann, 1898. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#hofmann #piano #rubinstein #musichistory #pianist

title: Mozart corrects his English pupil's homework
caption:
Attwood's papers document Mozart's teaching: exercises with the master's corrections and remarks. Attwood returned to London in 1787 and in 1796 became organist of St Paul's Cathedral. This page was reproduced in The Musical Times in 1900.

Image: Thomas Attwood and Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, figured bass exercise with Mozart's corrections, c. 1785. Attwood Papers, as reproduced in The Musical Times, 1900. Public domain.

#mozart #musicteacher #musiclessons #classicalmusic #musichistory

title: Goya's largest etching: a blind guitarist and his crowd
caption:
The tapestry cartoon had to be simplified, so this etching may be our best record of Goya's first idea. Few impressions survive, perhaps because the big plate was hard to print. Look at the faces around the guitarist, each listener reacting differently.

Image: Francisco de Goya, The Blind Guitarist, c. 1778. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. CC0.

#goya #guitar #printmaking #spain #arthistory #musichistory

title: Chez moi: Harriet Backer's room, with a pianist in blue
caption:
Harriet Backer called this 1887 painting Chez moi, at my place. Her sister Agathe became a celebrated pianist. Look at the daylight pouring through the window and the blue case waiting on the empty chair.

Image: Harriet Backer, Chez moi, 1887. Nasjonalmuseet, Oslo. Public domain.

#harrietbacker #womeninart #scandinavianart #arthistory #piano

title: Satie's golf piece: no bar lines, and a colonel in loud tweed
caption:
Satie wrote this page in his finest calligraphy, on red staves and without bar lines. Little phrases run between the notes: 'Le colonel est vêtu de Scotch Tweed d'un vert violent', the colonel is dressed in violent green tweed, and at the end his club flies to pieces. The album was composed in 1914 and published in 1923.

Image: Erik Satie, Sports et divertissements: Le golf (music page), composed 1914, published 1923. Houghton Library, Harvard University. Public domain.

#eriksatie #sportsetdivertissements #golf #sheetmusic #artdeco

title: The Swan Princess, painted by the singer's husband
caption:
Nadezhda Zabela-Vrubel was a coloratura soprano whose voice Rimsky-Korsakov greatly admired. Her husband Mikhail Vrubel designed the sets and costumes for The Tale of Tsar Saltan and painted this vision of her role in 1900.

Image: Mikhail Vrubel, The Swan Princess, 1900. State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow. Public domain.

#vrubel #rimskykorsakov #opera #russianart #arthistory #musichistory

title: Birds and insects painted inside a Paris harpsichord
caption:
French harpsichord soundboards were often painted, and this one carries flowers, insects and a bird around a cast metal rose. The gilded stand has seven curved cabriole legs. It was restored around 1900, when early instruments were being rediscovered.

Image: Louis Bellot, Harpsichord, 1742. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#harpsichord #rameau #baroque #musichistory #paris

title: Orpheus Britannicus: Purcell's songs, printed after his death
caption:
The title casts Purcell as a British Orpheus. In his preface Playford praises Purcell's way of setting English words. It was printed by John Heptinstall for Playford.

Image: Henry Purcell, Orpheus Britannicus, title page, London: Henry Playford, 1698. Internet Archive copy. Public domain.

#purcell #baroquemusic #englishsong #musichistory #firstedition

title: She played for Louis XIV at five. Then she wrote an opera
caption:
As a child she performed at Versailles and caught the king's eye. Her 1687 Pièces de clavecin was one of the few harpsichord books printed in France in that century. A writer of the time placed her on his French Parnassus beside Marais and Lalande, praising her improvised preludes.

Image: Louis Crépy, Élisabeth Jacquet de La Guerre (engraved portrait), 1729. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#jacquetdelaguerre #womenshistorymonth #harpsichord #baroque #musichistory

title: A violinist versus the street noise outside
audio_search: J. S. Bach, The Art of Fugue: Contrapunctus 1
caption:
Anyone who has tried to practice next to roadworks will know this face. Hogarth made the print as a companion to The Distrest Poet. Look at the window, then at the street below, and count the noise makers.

Image: William Hogarth, The Enraged Musician, 1741. Etching and engraving. Public domain.

#hogarth #violin #london #printmaking #arthistory #musichistory

title: The suite Saint-Saëns wouldn't let anyone publish
audio_search: Saint-Saëns, Caprice on Danish and Russian Airs, Op. 79
caption:
Saint-Saëns wrote this 14-movement suite in 1886 for private performance by two pianos and a small ensemble. It was published in 1922, the year after his death, and has been one of his most popular works ever since. This is the title page of his autograph.

Image: Camille Saint-Saëns, Le carnaval des animaux (autograph title page), 1886. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#saintsaens #carnivaloftheanimals #manuscript #theswan #frenchmusic

title: Grieg at the piano, his wife Nina singing
caption:
Grieg married Nina in 1867, and she became the great interpreter of his songs. Krøyer shows them as they performed together for friends, him at the keys, her standing to sing. Look for the date painted beside his signature.

Image: Peder Severin Krøyer, Edvard Grieg Accompanying His Wife, 1898. Nationalmuseum, Stockholm. Public domain.

#grieg #kroyer #scandinavianart #arthistory #musichistory #piano

title: A volume of Beethoven inlaid in a piano lid
caption:
Thomas Henry Foley commissioned it for his country house, Witley Court, to a design by George Henry Blake. The lid is covered in marquetry, and among the motifs is a book of Beethoven symphonies. Under the lid flap are the Foley family arms.

Image: Érard, designed by George Henry Blake, Grand Pianoforte, c. 1840. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#piano #erard #beethoven #marquetry #musichistory

title: A dance in paint, and the dance song below it
audio_search: Palestrina, Missa Papae Marcelli: Agnus Dei II
caption:
Guillaume de Machaut oversaw the making of manuscripts of his complete works. In the Remède de Fortune the story itself calls this song a chanson baladee, a dance song. Look for the castle at left, the dancers under the trees, and the red staff lines of the music below.

Image: Guillaume de Machaut, Remède de Fortune, 'Dame, a vous sans retollir', fol. 51r, c. 1350s. Bibliothèque nationale de France (Ms. fr. 1586). CC0.

#machaut #medievalmusic #illuminatedmanuscript #musichistory #virelai

title: Tuning up, with a cat for an audience
caption:
Every musician knows the pause before playing, when the tuning pegs get a last turn. Gakutei catches that moment and adds a cat staring at its own reflection. Look at her hand on the pegs of the long, slim neck.

Image: Yashima Gakutei, Woman Tuning a Shamisen and a Cat Looking at its Own Reflection, mid-1820s. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#shamisen #surimono #japaneseart #musichistory #cats

title: The song in her book matches no known piece
caption:
Bartolomeo Veneto and his workshop painted the notation carefully enough to read. It adds up to a tune, yet it has not been matched to any known song. Look at the open book, then at her hands on the lute.

Image: Bartolomeo Veneto and workshop, Lady Playing a Lute, about 1530. J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles. Public domain.

#bartolomeoveneto #lute #renaissance #arthistory #musichistory

title: Chopin's autograph of his Mazurka in B major, Op. 56 No. 1
audio_search: Chopin, Mazurka in B major, Op. 56 No. 1
caption:
Chopin wrote more than fifty mazurkas, turning a Polish village dance into concert music. Op. 56 has three, in B major, C major and C minor. This page is the start of No. 1 in Chopin's hand, from the collections shared online by the National Library of Poland.

Image: Frédéric Chopin, Mazurka in B major, Op. 56 No. 1 (autograph manuscript), 1843. Polona, National Library of Poland. Public domain.

#chopin #mazurka #manuscript #pianomusic #poland

title: Manet's first Salon success was a guitar player
caption:
Manet staged this singer in his Paris studio with props. The critic Théophile Gautier praised its true color and vigorous brush, and joked that the sitter was a guitarist from Montmartre. Look at the onions and the clay jug at his feet.

Image: Édouard Manet, The Spanish Singer, 1860. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#manet #guitar #arthistory #musichistory #metmuseum

title: The quiet keyboard composers practiced on
caption:
A clavichord's tangents stay on the string, so a player can rock a finger to make the note waver, an effect called Bebung. This is one of only two known clavichords by Kintzing, who worked with the cabinetmaker David Roentgen. Its case was painted gold in the 19th century.

Image: Attributed to Christian Kintzing, Clavichord, 1763. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#clavichord #cpebach #keyboard #musichistory #earlymusic

title: A queen's name hidden in the words: ELISABETH REGINA
audio_search: Josquin des Prez, Missa Pange lingua
caption:
This page is from the Lambeth Choirbook, also called the Arundel Choirbook, from around 1525. Each voice part starts with its own gilded letter E, and the name Fayrfax is written at the top. Look for the red notes mixed in with the black.

Image: Robert Fayrfax, Eterne laudis lilium, Lambeth Choirbook, fol. 56v, c. 1525. Lambeth Palace Library (MS 1). Public domain.

#fayrfax #tudormusic #choirbook #illuminatedmanuscript #musichistory

title: The drone that holds Indian music together
caption:
The Met describes her as a nayika, the ideal heroine of devotional poetry, with hints of Radha, Krishna's beloved. Her jewels and fine clothes mark her as a member of the court. Look at her fingers on the strings and the big round gourd resting at her lap.

Image: A Lady Playing the Tanpura, Kishangarh, Rajasthan, c. 1735. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Public domain.

#tanpura #indianart #rajput #arthistory #musichistory

title: Eight-year-old Mozart, playing at a Paris tea party
audio_search: Mozart, Piano Sonata in C, K. 330, finale
caption:
Tea is served English style, without servants, while the boy plays. The singer Jélyotte stands near him with a guitar. Conti, shut out of court, used the picture to show off his own salon of politics, letters and the arts.

Image: Michel-Barthélemy Ollivier, English Tea at the Temple, 1766. Musée national des châteaux de Versailles et de Trianon. Public domain.

#mozart #harpsichord #paris #rococo #arthistory #musichistory

title: Mozart's first symphony, written at age eight
caption:
Leopold needed silence, so the boy composed without playing an instrument. In the horns, listen for a four-note motif, C, D, F, E, that returns years later in the 'Jupiter' Symphony. The autograph is in the Jagiellonian Library in Kraków.

Image: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Symphony No. 1 in E-flat major, K. 16, autograph, f. 1r, 1764. Biblioteka Jagiellońska, Kraków. Public domain.

#mozart #symphony #classicalmusic #childprodigy #musichistory

title: Verdi in a top hat, drawn by Boldini in pastel
caption:
Giovanni Boldini was famous for fast, dashing portraits. Here Verdi, in his seventies, wears a top hat and a striped silk scarf. Look at the top right corner, where Boldini wrote 'Parigi 9 April 1886'.

Image: Giovanni Boldini, Portrait of Giuseppe Verdi, 1886. Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna, Rome. Public domain.

#verdi #boldini #opera #arthistory #musichistory

title: Artemisia Gentileschi, painting herself as a musician
caption:
Gentileschi cast herself as a performer, lute in hand, rather than as a painter at the easel. She made it while working in Florence, where the Medici were among her patrons.

Image: Artemisia Gentileschi, Self-Portrait as a Lute Player, c. 1615-17. Wadsworth Atheneum Museum of Art, Hartford. Public domain.

#artemisiagentileschi #womeninart #lute #baroque #arthistory #musichistory

title: Augusta Holmès writes the anthem for the 1889 World's Fair
caption:
