Holmès wrote the words to almost all of her vocal music herself, and this title page says it plainly: 'poème et musique par Augusta Holmès'. Below, she notes it is the orchestral score, 'manuscrit original'. A stamp at the top marks it as part of her bequest.

Image: Augusta Holmès, Ode triomphale en l'honneur du Centenaire de 1789 (autograph full score, title page), 1889. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#augustaholmes #womencomposers #manuscript #paris1889 #frenchmusic

title: Klimt's first painting called Music, 1895
caption:
Years before his famous gold portraits, Klimt painted Music as a woman in a dark dress playing a golden lyre. Look for the stone sphinx at the right edge and the mask at the left.

Image: Gustav Klimt, Music, 1895. Neue Pinakothek, Munich. Public domain.

#klimt #vienna #symbolism #arthistory #musichistory

title: A sunburst of silk on an upright piano
audio_search: Chopin, Nocturne in E-flat, Op. 55 No. 2
caption:
Tall cabinet pianos saved floor space in city parlors. The pleated silk panel spreads out like a sunburst. Firth, Hall & Pond mainly published and sold music, so a contracted maker probably built it.

Image: Firth, Hall & Pond, Upright Cabinet Piano, 1835. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#piano #uprightpiano #newyork #americanart #musichistory

title: Satie's Gnossienne No. 5, in his hand, 1889
caption:
Satie invented the word 'Gnossienne' for these pieces. He often left out bar lines and time signatures and wrote odd instructions instead of tempo markings. This is the first page of his autograph of No. 5, from the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Image: Erik Satie, Gnossienne No. 5 (autograph, first page), 1889. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#eriksatie #gnossienne #manuscript #pianomusic #frenchmusic

title: She sang, and the peacock danced
caption:
Ragamala painters gave each musical mode a mood and a scene. Here longing is the mood: the heroine sings in praise of her beloved, and even the peacock is moved. Look for the vina in her right hand and the pair of yellow birds taking flight.

Image: Woman Addressing a Peacock: Gujari Ragini of Megh, from a Ragamala, Bundi or Raghogarh, c. 1680. Cleveland Museum of Art. CC0.

#ragamala #indianart #raga #vina #arthistory

title: A ring of angels, ringing bells and playing instruments
caption:
The outer circle of angels plays instruments and waves bells, while an inner six hold the instruments of Christ's Passion. Zoom in and try to name every instrument you can spot.

Image: Geertgen tot Sint Jans, The Glorification of the Virgin, c. 1490-95. Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, Rotterdam. Public domain.

#geertgentotsintjans #angels #earlymusic #arthistory #musichistory

title: Six concertos for a margrave, dated March 24, 1721
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Fugue No. 15 in G major, BWV 860
caption:
After the margrave's death the score passed to Bach's pupil Kirnberger, then to Princess Anna Amalia, and reached Berlin's Royal Library in 1914. In World War II a librarian escaped a bombing raid with the scores hidden under his coat. They are now in the Berlin State Library.

Image: Johann Sebastian Bach, Six Concerts avec plusieurs instruments (Brandenburg Concertos), dedication title page, 1721. Berlin State Library. Public domain.

#bach #brandenburgconcertos #baroquemusic #musichistory #manuscript

title: Liszt at 28, by Henri Lehmann
caption:
Before he was a white-haired abbé, Liszt was the long-haired star of the concert hall. Lehmann paints him standing, arms folded, face turned over his shoulder toward us.

Image: Henri Lehmann, Portrait of Franz Liszt, 1839. Musée Carnavalet, Paris. CC0.

#liszt #portrait #romanticism #arthistory #musichistory #piano

title: A Schubert evening, drawn from memory 40 years later
audio_search: Schubert, Sonata in E-flat, D. 568, Menuetto
caption:
Schubert sits at the piano with the singer Johann Michael Vogl beside him, surrounded by friends. Look at the portrait on the wall behind them: Countess Karoline Esterházy.

Image: Moritz von Schwind, Schubertiade, 1868. Wien Museum, Vienna. Public domain.

#schubert #schubertiade #vienna #arthistory #musichistory #piano

title: Opus 1: Schubert's Erlkönig in print, 1821
caption:
One singer voices four characters: narrator, father, son and the Erlking. Under them, the pianist keeps up relentless repeated octaves and chords in triplets. The first public performance was on March 7, 1821, at the Theater am Kärntnertor in Vienna.

Image: Franz Schubert, Erlkönig, Op. 1, D. 328, first edition title page, Vienna: Diabelli, 1821. IMSLP scan. Public domain.

#schubert #erlkonig #lied #firstedition #musichistory

title: One of the oldest violins, maybe made for a royal wedding
caption:
Andrea Amati shaped the violin family as we know it. This one is painted with fleurs-de-lis and a Latin motto about religion's single bulwark. The royal set is a possibility, not a certainty.

Image: Andrea Amati, Ex "Kurtz" Violin, c. 1560. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#violin #amati #cremona #renaissance #musichistory

title: A koto lesson disguised as a landscape
caption:
The classic Chinese theme "Wild Geese Descending on a Sandbank" becomes a girl practicing the koto. Look at the movable bridges under the strings: their diagonal line is the flock of geese coming in to land. The series is often called the first set of full-color Japanese woodblock prints.

Image: Suzuki Harunobu, Geese Descending on the Koto Bridges (Eight Parlor Views), c. 1766. Rijksmuseum. Public domain.

#koto #harunobu #ukiyoe #japaneseart #musichistory

title: Cécile Chaminade, on the sheet music for Suédoise, 1911
caption:
Publishers put Chaminade's photograph on her music because buyers knew her name and her face. This image comes from the 1911 sheet music for her piece Suédoise. In 1913 she became the first woman composer awarded the Légion d'honneur.

Image: Cécile Chaminade, from the sheet music for Suédoise, c. 1911. Internet Archive. Public domain.

#chaminade #womencomposers #sheetmusic #pianomusic #1911

title: Two singing sisters, painted by Gainsborough
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Prelude No. 19 in A major, BWV 864
caption:
The sisters pose together outdoors, one seated with a music book on her lap. In 1785 the family asked Gainsborough to repaint their dresses in the latest fashion, and he did. Their brother William gave the picture to Dulwich in 1835.

Image: Thomas Gainsborough, Elizabeth and Mary Linley, 1772. Dulwich Picture Gallery, London. Public domain.

#gainsborough #singers #georgian #arthistory #musichistory

title: Violin, piano, cello and baton. Carnegie Hall, 1917
caption:
Kreisler wrote many charming violin pieces and passed them off as works by Pugnani, Tartini and Vivaldi. When he admitted it, he answered critics: 'The name changes, the value remains.' Here he stands with three other stars of New York concert life.

Image: Bain News Service, Fritz Kreisler, Harold Bauer, Pablo Casals and Walter Damrosch at Carnegie Hall, 1917. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#kreisler #casals #violin #carnegiehall #musichistory

title: Signed 'Elizabeth Jacquet', to Louis XIV
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Prelude No. 20 in A minor, BWV 865
caption:
The book held harpsichord pieces that can also be played on the violin, and six sonatas for violin and harpsichord. In the letter she reminds the king that he 'did not disdain' her childhood. Look for 'Au Roy' at the top and her signature at bottom right.

Image: Élisabeth Jacquet de La Guerre, Pièces de clavecin qui peuvent se jouer sur le viollon, dedication, 1707. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#jacquetdelaguerre #womencomposers #baroquemusic #harpsichord #musichistory

title: Young Erik Satie, painted on a Paris street in 1891
caption:
Satie had written his three Gymnopédies in 1888 and was playing piano at the Chat Noir cabaret. Ramon Casas painted him in a top hat and long coat in the gray winter light. Look for the windmill behind him and the pince-nez on its cord.

Image: Ramon Casas, El bohemi (Erik Satie), 1891. Collection to confirm. Public domain.

#satie #ramoncasas #montmartre #arthistory #musichistory

title: Leighton named a painting after Mendelssohn's Songs Without Words
caption:
Frederic Leighton's title, Lieder ohne Worte, points to music without saying a word. It invites you to listen to a painting.

Image: Frederic Leighton, Lieder ohne Worte, c. 1861. Tate, London. Public domain.

#mendelssohn #leighton #victorianart #arthistory #musichistory #piano

title: A Song Without Words, for four hands
caption:
Mendelssohn's Lieder ohne Worte are songs for the piano alone, with the melody singing over the accompaniment. His sister Fanny wrote pieces in the same genre. This manuscript sets one of them for two players at one piano.

Image: Felix Mendelssohn, Lied ohne Worte für das Piano vierhändig (manuscript), 1847. Google Arts & Culture. Public domain.

#mendelssohn #songswithoutwords #manuscript #pianoduet #romanticera

title: The London composer welcomed at the White House
audio_search: Dvořák, Goin' Home (Largo from the 'New World')
caption:
In Washington, D.C., a 200-voice African American chorus named itself the Samuel Coleridge-Taylor Society in 1901. He toured the United States three times, in 1904, 1906 and 1910. He died in 1912, aged just 37.

Image: Photographer unknown, Samuel Coleridge-Taylor, c. 1905. Public domain.

#coleridgetaylor #blackhistory #composer #britishmusic #musichistory

title: The harpsichord tourists came to Rome to see
audio_search: J. S. Bach, The Art of Fugue: Contrapunctus 5
caption:
Todini designed it, Basilio Onofri gilded it and Jacob Reiff carved it. The carved frieze tells the story of the sea nymph Galatea and the giant Polyphemus, who loved her. In the 1670s, visitors to Rome paid calls on Todini's gallery of musical machines to see it.

Image: Michele Todini, Basilio Onofri and Jacob Reiff, Harpsichord, c. 1670. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#harpsichord #baroque #rome #musichistory #arthistory

title: Before it was a Liebestraum, it was a song
caption:
The three Liebesträume for piano started life as songs. This copy of Gestorben war ich was made for the Leipzig publisher Kistner, and Liszt added changes in ink and red pencil. Top right he wrote 'Gedicht von Uhland', poem by Uhland; the big 1755 at the top is the engraver's plate number.

Image: Franz Liszt, Gestorben war ich (copyist's manuscript with Liszt's autograph additions), c. 1845-50. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#liszt #liebestraum #manuscript #artsong #romanticera

title: A musical mode, painted as a woman with deer
caption:
In a ragamala, each painting stands for one raga or ragini, with a verse naming it in the border. Todi is shown as a lone woman holding a vina while deer come close to her. Look for the Sanskrit verse in the yellow band at the top.

Image: Woman Feeding Deer: Todi Ragini, from a Ragamala, Amber, c. 1610. Cleveland Museum of Art. CC0.

#ragamala #indianart #raga #vina #musichistory

title: The choir that sang a university into being
caption:
In 1873 the group sang "Steal Away to Jesus" and "Go Down, Moses" for Queen Victoria. This group portrait was printed as the frontispiece of a book in the 1870s. Among the faces are Ella Sheppard, Maggie Porter and Thomas Rutling.

Image: Anonymous, Group Portrait of the Jubilee Singers (Woodburytype), 1872 to 1877. Rijksmuseum. CC0.

#fiskjubileesingers #blackhistory #spirituals #choir #musichistory

title: Couperin's second harpsichord book, Paris, 1717
caption:
The title page lists his posts: organist of the King's Chapel and former teacher of the late Dauphin, Duke of Burgundy. Copies were sold at his own home near the church of Saint-Gervais, where he was organist. Look for the printed price: 18 livres.

Image: François Couperin, Second Livre de pièces de clavecin, title page, Paris, 1717. IMSLP scan. Public domain.

#couperin #harpsichord #baroquemusic #musichistory #firstedition

title: Venice puts on a concert for Russia's future tsar
audio_search: Scarlatti, Sonata in G major, K. 146
caption:
The choir and orchestra of the Ospedale della Pietà performed for the state guests in a hall of the Old Procurators' Offices. The royal visitors sit opposite the musicians' gallery. Look up to find the performers, then down at the glittering crowd.

Image: Francesco Guardi, Venetian Gala Concert, 1782. Alte Pinakothek, Munich. Public domain.

#guardi #venice #concert #rococo #arthistory #musichistory

title: Ten court ladies, one long table, a whole band
caption:
Some of the ladies drink tea and some drink wine, and nearly everyone else is playing. The bamboo table, crescent stools and floral headdresses all point to late Tang taste. Look under the table for the dog, then count the instruments.

Image: Anonymous, A Palace Concert, Tang dynasty (late Tang style). National Palace Museum, Taipei. Public domain.

#chineseart #tangdynasty #lunarnewyear #pipa #musichistory

title: Schumann's sketch for Einsame Blumen, from Forest Scenes
caption:
Waldszenen is a set of nine short piano pieces, first published in Leipzig in 1850-51. Schumann defended giving music titles, as long as they were apt. This draft of 'Einsame Blumen' belongs to the Austrian National Library in Vienna.

Image: Robert Schumann, Waldszenen, Op. 82 No. 3 'Einsame Blumen' (autograph draft), 1848-49. Austrian National Library. CC0.

#schumann #waldszenen #manuscript #pianomusic #romanticera

title: Renoir met Wagner in 1882. This is what he saw
audio_search: Chopin, Étude Op. 10 No. 9 in F minor
caption:
Wagner completed Parsifal in Palermo in January 1882, and Renoir painted him that same year. The result is quick and soft, nothing like the stern Wagner of photographs. Look at the feathery brushwork around the head.

Image: Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Richard Wagner, 1882. Musée d'Orsay, Paris. Public domain.

#wagner #renoir #impressionism #arthistory #musichistory

title: A harpsichord held up by crowned mermaids
audio_search: J. S. Bach, The Art of Fugue: Contrapunctus 2
caption:
The front legs rest on mermaids wearing crowns, a device of the powerful Roman Colonna family. The lid shows a landscape with a hunter and his dog. Above the keys, look for Tobias walking with the angel Raphael.

Image: Italian maker, Harpsichord, late 17th century. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#harpsichord #baroque #italianart #musichistory #earlymusic

title: The blind organist of Florence, in a golden initial
caption:
The codex was made in Florence around 1410 to 1415 and holds 354 Italian songs. Landini has 146 complete pieces in it, the largest surviving collection of his music. Each composer's section opens with an illuminated portrait.

Image: Anonymous, Squarcialupi Codex, page 246, c. 1410-1415. Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Florence. Public domain.

#landini #medievalmusic #illuminatedmanuscript #musichistory #florence

title: An Egyptian artist's practice sketch of a harpist
caption:
Ostraca were flakes of stone or pottery used as scrap paper. The artist laid down a pale red draft and then went over it in darker red with short strokes. It was found in 1922 to 1923 near a tomb at Deir el-Bahri.

Image: Ostracon with sketch of a harpist, Egypt, Dynasty 26, c. 664 to 610 BCE. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#harp #ancientegypt #drawing #arthistory #musichistory

title: He heard a piece once and could play it back
caption:
Promoters toured him from the age of eight, sometimes four shows a day, and the family that held him kept most of what he earned. He was also a composer of piano pieces. This photograph shows him around 1880.

Image: Blind Tom (Thomas Wiggins), c. 1880. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#blindtom #blackhistory #pianist #piano #musichistory

title: A Chaminade song to words by the first Nobel laureate in literature
caption:
The cover frames the title with a dark tree and a single bird on a branch. It names the poet, Sully Prudhomme, and 'C. Chaminade', and was published by Enoch Frères & Costallat in Paris. Chaminade went on to become the first woman composer awarded the Légion d'honneur, in 1913.

Image: P. Borie (cover), Cécile Chaminade, L'idéal, Enoch Frères & Costallat, 1888. HathiTrust. Public domain.

#chaminade #womencomposers #sheetmusic #frenchmusic #artsong

title: Three singers, one lute, and a woman keeping time
caption:
The man in the middle plays the lute, and the man behind strains for his note. A rebec and a recorder lie close at hand. The song may be a frottola, the popular part-song of Italian courts.

Image: Lorenzo Costa, A Concert, about 1488-90. National Gallery, London. Public domain.

#lorenzocosta #renaissance #singing #lute #arthistory #musichistory

title: Manet married his brothers' piano teacher
caption:
Suzanne played Schumann and Wagner, and Manet painted her at home in profile, hands on the keys. He chose a high viewpoint so her hands stay in view. Look in the mirror behind her for a clock and a pair of candlesticks.

Image: Édouard Manet, Madame Manet at the Piano, 1867–68. Musée d'Orsay, Paris. Public domain.

#manet #piano #impressionism #arthistory #musichistory #pianoteacher

title: Paris, around 1200: Pérotin's Alleluia Nativitas
caption:
Pérotin worked in Paris around 1200 and is counted the leading composer of the Notre Dame school of polyphony. Almost all we know of him comes from that late 13th-century English student. This copy is in a manuscript at the Herzog August Bibliothek in Wolfenbüttel, Germany.

Image: Pérotin, Alleluia Nativitas, Codex Guelf. 1099, manuscript copy. Herzog August Bibliothek, Wolfenbüttel. Public domain.

#perotin #notredame #medievalmusic #musichistory #manuscript

title: A guitar shaped like Apollo's lyre
audio_search: Chopin, Étude Op. 10 No. 9 in F minor
caption:
Lyre guitars were a Neoclassical fashion, made to look like the instruments on ancient vases. Its label reads 'Pons fils luthier'. In London, Edward Light sold a rival harp-lute he called the 'Apollo' from 1811.

Image: Possibly Joseph Pons, Lyre Guitar, c. 1805. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#guitar #lyreguitar #neoclassical #musichistory #instruments

title: Judith Leyster signed this one with a star
caption:
The star is a pun on her name: leidster means lodestar. For two centuries her paintings were credited to Frans Hals or Jan Miense Molenaer, until she was rediscovered in 1893. Look at the lute held close as he sings.

Image: Judith Leyster, The Serenade, 1629. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Public domain.

#judithleyster #womeninart #lute #dutchgoldenage #arthistory #musichistory

title: Kismet Rag, 1913: the Sphinx, two snakes and a magic lamp
caption:
Ragtime publishers sold music with eye-catching covers, and this one leans into the craze for all things Egyptian. The Sphinx sits in a medallion, ringed by two golden snakes, with an oil lamp up in the corner. Only Joplin's name is on the cover, although Scott Hayden is usually credited as his co-composer.

Image: H. Reichard (cover), Kismet Rag by Scott Joplin and Scott Hayden, Stark Music Co., 1913. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#scottjoplin #ragtime #sheetmusic #kismetrag #pianomusic

title: A blue goddess playing a bowed lute, in silk and gold
caption:
She stands on a lotus with a rainbow halo, drawing a bow across her lute. The piece is embroidered in silk and gold thread and was once part of a much larger hanging. Look at the ruffled hem and the scarves that seem to float.

Image: Celestial Musician, Central Asia, 14th century. Cleveland Museum of Art. CC0.

#textileart #buddhistart #centralasia #arthistory #musichistory

title: Vermeer's guitar player was once held for ransom
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Prelude No. 19 in A major, BWV 864
caption:
A young woman strums a guitar and glances away to one side, as if someone just out of frame is listening. Thieves took the painting from Kenwood in 1974 and demanded a ransom before it was recovered. It has hung there since the Iveagh Bequest in the 1920s.

Image: Johannes Vermeer, The Guitar Player, c. 1672. Kenwood House, London (Iveagh Bequest). Public domain.

#vermeer #guitar #dutchgoldenage #arthistory #musichistory

title: The book that taught harmony to think in chords, 1722
caption:
Rameau was about 38, and the title page calls him organist of Clermont Cathedral. It was printed by Ballard, the king's sole music printer. His first opera, Hippolyte et Aricie, came only at 50.

Image: Jean-Philippe Rameau, Traité de l'harmonie, title page, Paris: Ballard, 1722. Copy not named on Commons. Public domain.

#rameau #musictheory #baroquemusic #harmony #musichistory

title: Anders Zorn's old fiddler, Hins Anders
audio_search: Schubert, Sonata in A, D. 664, Andante
caption:
Swedish painter Anders Zorn shows an old fiddler deep in a tune, in a red and blue cap and pale coat, against a log wall. Look at the bow hand and the weathered face bent toward the strings.

Image: Anders Zorn, Hins Anders, 1904. Thiel Gallery, Stockholm. Public domain.

#anderszorn #fiddle #scandinavianart #folkmusic #arthistory

title: Violinist, composer, conductor and champion fencer
audio_search: Beethoven, String Quartet Op. 18 No. 6, Scherzo
caption:
Saint-Georges was the son of a planter and Nanon, an enslaved woman. In Paris he beat the best swordsmen of his day, led the Concert des Amateurs and wrote some of the first string quartets in France. This 1788 engraving copies a portrait that hung in Henry Angelo's fencing academy in London.

Image: William Ward after Mather Brown, Monsieur de St. George, 1788. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#saintgeorges #blackhistory #violin #composer #musichistory

title: Haydn's draft of a tune Germany still sings
audio_search: Haydn, 'Lark' Quartet, Op. 64 No. 5, first movement
caption:
The words are by Lorenz Leopold Haschka, and this draft carries all four stanzas. Haydn reused the tune for variations in his 'Emperor' Quartet, Op. 76 No. 3, and in May 1809 it was the last music he ever played. The melody now carries the third stanza of Germany's national anthem.

Image: Joseph Haydn, Gott erhalte Franz den Kaiser, draft, c. 1796-1797. Austrian National Library. Public domain.

#haydn #anthem #classicalmusic #musichistory #manuscript

title: A piano believed to be Napoleon's wife's
caption:
Marie Louise kept it as Duchess of Parma, according to the museum. Look for the gilt mounts of grapevines, Psyche at a brazier and imperial eagles, and the milk-glass name plaque. Its carved griffin pedal support was lost in World War II.

Image: Joseph Böhm, Grand Piano, c. 1815–20. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#piano #fortepiano #vienna #napoleon #musichistory

title: King Alfonso's songbook, with a portrait of the band
audio_search: Palestrina, Missa Papae Marcelli: Agnus Dei I
caption:
Alfonso X of Castile gathered more than 400 songs to the Virgin in Galician-Portuguese, with music. This copy breaks its pages with pictures of players and their instruments. Here one musician bows a rebab while his partner plucks a lute.

Image: Cantigas de Santa Maria, Codex of the Musicians (Escorial b.I.2), fol. 162r, early 1280s. Real Biblioteca del Monasterio de El Escorial. Public domain.

#medievalmusic #cantigas #manuscript #lute #musichistory

title: The last bars of Tristan und Isolde, in Wagner's hand
audio_search: Schubert, Sonata in A, D. 664, finale
caption:
Wagner wrote both the words and the music of this three-act music drama, inspired in part by Schopenhauer and his love for Mathilde Wesendonck. Here are the closing bars, reproduced in facsimile from his manuscript. It ends with Isolde's Liebestod.

Image: Richard Wagner, Tristan und Isolde, final bars (facsimile of the autograph), 1859. Frankfurt University Library, Manskopf collection. Public domain.

#wagner #tristanundisolde #manuscript #opera #liebestod

title: Young Rembrandt, putting himself in the band
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Prelude No. 20 in A minor, BWV 865
caption:
A viola da gamba, a harp, a lute and a violin all appear in this early scene. The Rijksmuseum bought it in 1976. During the war it had been earmarked for Hitler's planned museum in Linz.

Image: Rembrandt van Rijn, Musical Company, 1626. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Public domain.

#rembrandt #dutchgoldenage #violadagamba #harp #arthistory #musichistory

title: A serenade for someone we never see
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Fugue No. 20 in A minor, BWV 865
caption:
Mezzetin was a lovesick character from the Italian comedy. He strums his guitar and lifts his face toward a window we can't see, while the stone Venus in the garden turns away. Catherine the Great once owned the painting; the Met bought it in 1934.

Image: Antoine Watteau, Mezzetin, c. 1718-20. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. CC0.

#watteau #guitar #serenade #rococo #arthistory #musichistory

title: Debussy asked for Hokusai's wave on the cover of La mer
audio_search: Debussy, La mer: From Dawn to Noon on the Sea
caption:
Debussy composed La mer between 1903 and 1905, and the first edition carried a version of Hokusai's Great Wave off Kanagawa. Early listeners were unsure, even some of his supporters. After a second Paris performance in 1908, it quickly became one of his most played works.

Image: Claude Debussy, La mer, first edition cover (Durand), 1905. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#debussy #lamer #hokusai #sheetmusic #impressionism

title: A violin serenade from the top of a ladder
audio_search: Schubert, Sonata in A, D. 664, Andante
caption:
Carl Spitzweg painted small, gently funny scenes of German town life. Here a violinist climbs a ladder on a rooftop to play up toward a window box of flowers. Look at the stormy blue sky behind him.

Image: Carl Spitzweg, Ständchen (Serenade), 1854. Private collection. Public domain.

#spitzweg #serenade #violin #biedermeier #arthistory #musichistory

title: The Blue Danube was first sung, not danced
audio_search: Johann Strauss II, The Blue Danube
caption:
The orchestral version came later and conquered the world. Viennese artist Hans Schließmann, known for his portraits of musicians, caught Strauss in silhouette. Watch the posture: violin up, all motion.

Image: Hans Schließmann, Johann Strauss II (silhouette), before 1920. Public domain.

#johannstrauss #bluedanube #waltz #vienna #musichistory

title: An early printing of The Blue Danube, Vienna, 1867
audio_search: Johann Strauss II, The Blue Danube
caption:
Johann Strauss II wrote An der schönen blauen Donau, Op. 314, as a choral waltz for the Vienna Men's Choral Association. The first performance in 1867 went only fairly well. His orchestral version for the Paris World's Fair that year became a hit. This edition was published by C. A. Spina in Vienna.

Image: Johann Strauss II, An der schönen blauen Donau, Op. 314 (C. A. Spina edition), 1867. Collection Walter Anton. Public domain.

#johannstrauss #bluedanube #waltz #sheetmusic #vienna

title: Half harp, half piano, all on show
caption:
John Stewart patented the euphonicon in 1841. Instead of hiding the strings in a case, it shows off the iron frame in a harp-like shape. The case is Macassar ebony.

Image: F. Beale & Co., Upright Harp Piano (Euphonicon), 1843. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#piano #harp #victorian #musichistory #instruments

title: The first woman to win the Prix de Rome, baton in hand
caption:
The Prix de Rome was France's top prize for young composers, and no woman had won it before. Boulanger died in 1918 at only 24. Her piano piece D'un jardin clair dates from 1914.

Image: Pascal Dagnan-Bouveret, Lili Boulanger conducting her cantata Faust et Hélène, 1913. Public domain.

#liliboulanger #womenshistorymonth #composer #conducting #musichistory

title: Mozart's 'dice game' page, with every bar lettered
audio_search: Mozart, Piano Concerto No. 22, K. 482, opening
caption:
The fragments have no instructions, and nothing proves dice were used, though a dice game sold under Mozart's name appeared in 1792. Look for the letters written under the bars. At the top a later note reads 'Von Mozart und seiner Handschrift': by Mozart, in his hand.

Image: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, String Quintet K. 516 (piano reduction fragment) and Musikalisches Würfelspiel, K. 516f, autograph, 1787. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Public domain.

#mozart #dicegame #classicalmusic #composition #musichistory

title: A Vermeer that has been missing since 1990
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Fugue No. 23 in B major, BWV 868
caption:
Vermeer painted this trio of musicians in a Delft interior around 1664: a woman at the keyboard, a man with a lute, a woman singing. It is thought to be the most valuable stolen work still unrecovered. Look for the viola da gamba lying on the floor, waiting for a player who never comes.

Image: Johannes Vermeer, The Concert, c. 1664. Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston (stolen 1990). Public domain.

#vermeer #dutchgoldenage #harpsichord #arthistory #musichistory

title: Arcangelo Corelli, the prince of musicians
audio_search: J. S. Bach, Goldberg Variations: Variation 8
caption:
Admirers called him the prince of musicians. His Concerto Grosso Op. 6 No. 8, with its pastorale finale, was written for Christmas Eve. This portrait is attributed to the Irish painter Hugh Howard.

Image: Attributed to Hugh Howard, Arcangelo Corelli. Royal Society of Musicians of Great Britain. Public domain.

#corelli #violin #composer #baroque #arthistory #musichistory

title: Op. 109, written for Maximiliane Brentano
audio_search: Beethoven, Moonlight Sonata, Op. 27 No. 2, finale
caption:
This is the first page of the first movement, Vivace ma non troppo. The finale is a theme with six variations marked 'Gesangvoll, mit innigster Empfindung', songful, with deepest feeling. Beethoven sent his hard-to-read autograph to the publisher Schlesinger in Berlin.

Image: Ludwig van Beethoven, Piano Sonata No. 30 in E major, Op. 109, autograph, first page, 1820. Library of Congress. Public domain.

#beethoven #pianosonata #piano #classicalmusic #musichistory

title: The 369th's band marches home up Fifth Avenue, 1919
audio_search: H. Taylor Weeks, Mew Mew Rag (1910)
caption:
The original caption called it the best band in the American Expeditionary Forces and said General Pershing borrowed it for a month. Before the war, Europe's Clef Club played Carnegie Hall in 1912. He wrote dances, including the Castle Walk, for Vernon and Irene Castle.

Image: Western Newspaper Union, Lt. James Europe and his Famous Jazz Band of the 369th, 1919. U.S. National Archives. Public domain.

#jamesreeseeurope #jazz #harlemhellfighters #blackhistory #musichistory

title: A swarbat, painted by India's Raja Ravi Varma
caption:
Raja Ravi Varma blended European oil technique with Indian subjects, and in 1894 he set up a press to print his pictures. Here a woman in a gold sari and blue blouse holds a swarbat, a plucked string instrument. Look at the jewelry and the two sound holes in the instrument's round body.

Image: Raja Ravi Varma, A Tamil Lady Playing the Swarbat, after the 1874 original. Kowdiar Palace, Thiruvananthapuram. Public domain.

#rajaravivarma #indianart #swarbat #arthistory #musichistory

title: 'Du holde Kunst': Schubert's song of thanks to music
audio_search: Schubert, Sonata in A, D. 664, finale
caption:
A decade after writing it, on April 24, 1827, Schubert dedicated the song to the Viennese pianist Albert Sowinsky. Look for both verses written under one vocal line, and Schubert's signature at top right. This facsimile was printed in 1913.

Image: Franz Schubert, An die Musik, D. 547, manuscript, facsimile published by W. Dahms, 1913. Public domain.

#schubert #lied #andiemusik #classicalmusic #musichistory

title: A serpent with keys: the ophicleide
caption:
Its name comes from Greek words for 'serpent' and 'key'. Berlioz wrote for it in the Symphonie fantastique, and Mendelssohn used it in Elijah. By the end of the century the tuba and euphonium had taken its place.

Image: Bartsch, Bass Ophicleide, 1837–54. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.

#ophicleide #berlioz #instruments #musichistory #brass

title: Six musicians and one dancing boy, Korea, 1700s
audio_search: Ravel, Miroirs: Une barque sur l'océan
caption:
Kim Hong-do, known by his art name Danwon, is famous for his album of genre scenes. The players sit in a half circle around the dancer. Find the haegeum, a two-string fiddle, and the hourglass drum.

Image: Kim Hong-do, A Dancing Boy (Album of Genre Paintings), late 18th century. National Museum of Korea. Public domain.
